item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Economic Inclusion Initiatives Promote Entrepreneurship, Livelihoods and Rehabilitation Among Marginalised Communities
Over Rs 613 Crore Approved for 145 Companies under VCF-SC; Nearly Rs 143 Crore Approved for 31 Companies under VCF-BC
Investments Create Assets Worth Nearly Rs 800 Crore and Generate Around 4,500 Employment Opportunities
More than Rs 46 Crore Released for Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in Begging
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, through its Economic Inclusion Division (EID), is strengthening entrepreneurship, livelihood generation and rehabilitation support for marginalised communities.

Its major initiatives include the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), the Venture Capital Fund for Backward Classes and the comprehensive rehabilitation component for persons engaged in begging under the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise Scheme.

Deputy Director General, Economic Inclusion Division (EID), in the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Ms Pratima Gupta informed that under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) with a total corpus of Rs 750 crore, the Fund provides financial assistance ranging from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore at an interest rate of 4 per cent.

She said from FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, the Fund has played an important role in enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish businesses, create productive assets and generate employment.

DDG EID further said that as of May 2026, the financial assistance of Rs 613.02 crore had been approved for 145 companies under the fund. Of this, Rs 437.74 crore had been disbursed to 123 companies, she added.

Ms Gupta said VCF-SC aims to promote entrepreneurship among members of Scheduled Caste communities by providing concessional financial assistance for establishing and expanding commercially viable enterprises.

The DDG EID said under VCF-SC, the Ministry launched the Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission (ASIIM) on September 30, 2020 that supports innovative ideas developed by young Scheduled Caste researchers and students by providing financial assistance of up to Rs 30 lakh.

She added that under ASIIM, an amount of Rs 29.11 crore has been sanctioned to 114 companies, while Rs 13.27 crore has been disbursed to 91 companies wherein the Mission seeks to encourage technology-driven and socially relevant enterprises while developing an ecosystem of innovation among young entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Caste communities.

Talking about the Venture Capital Fund for Backward Classes (VCF-BC), the DDG EID said it was launched in October 2019 to promote entrepreneurship among individuals belonging to Backward Classes. With a corpus of Rs 200 crore, the fund provides financial assistance ranging from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 15 crore at an interest rate of 6 per cent, she further said.

Ms Gupta said financial assistance of Rs 142.88 crore has been approved for 31 companies, of which Rs 70.23 crore has been disbursed to 19 companies, as of now.

The DDG EID said Venture Capital Funds have supported 329 Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs and 35 entrepreneurs belonging to Backward Classes adding these investments have collectively generated around 4,500 direct and indirect employment opportunities.

She said the enterprises supported through these Funds have created permanent productive assets valued at nearly Rs 800 crores that are expected to contribute to economic activity, infrastructure development and employment generation over the next 12 to 15 years.

Ms Pratima further said as part of implementing the comprehensive rehabilitation component for persons engaged in begging under the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) Scheme, the Ministry follows a comprehensive approach encompassing identification, mobilisation, rescue, shelter, counselling, healthcare, education, skill development, livelihood support and reintegration of persons engaged in begging.

The DDG EID said from the launch of the initiative on October 23, 2023 through FY 2025-26, the central assistance amounting to Rs 46.16 crore was released. Of this, an amount of Rs 27.17 crore was released during FY 2025-26 alone, she added.

Ms Pratima said through these initiatives, the Economic Inclusion Division is advancing the Government's commitment to social justice by enabling entrepreneurship, supporting enterprise creation, generating employment and facilitating the dignified rehabilitation and economic inclusion of marginalised communities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi
The roadmap of drug-free India is very important to achieve Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's goal of creating a Viksit Bharat by 2047
The time has come to take a strong and decisive blow on narcotics, which have become a serious threat to the country and the world
With the aim of improving the welfare of the youth of the whole world, we have prepared the roadmap 2029
By 2029 we will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India
Neither will we allow a single gram of drugs to enter India, nor will we allow a single gram of drugs to go out of India, this is the aim to move ahead
We have to fight together and win by making the fight against drugs a top priority with compassion
In this fight against drugs, we are moving towards complete victory by setting TARGET, TIMELINE and ACCOUNTABILITY
Now we have to go from MEETING to MISSION, REPORTING to RESULT, SEIZURE to END OF NETWORK and CASE to CONVICTION
Our goal should be to make ANTF an Anti Narco Mission Command
Move forward with the aim of dismantling the network instead of a Seizure-centric approach
District will have to be made the basic unit of fight against drugs
Nashamukt Mitras will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges and institutions of the country to create awareness among the youth and sensitize the campus directors
Along with backward-forward investigation, financial investigation and finding digital links should be our priority
The cartel has to be attacked at three levels - entry point, interstate distribution system and local cell network in the districts
The districts will be divided into three clusters – drug manufacturing or entry districts, transportation corridor districts and consumption districts
A campaign will have to be launched to send back the foreign accused present in India and blacklist them, so that they cannot come to India again
The fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts
Make the entire process of converting every ANTF information into actionable intelligence a part of your state's police culture
Union Home Minister launched TVCs for anti-narcotics awareness, launched NCB website and laid foundation stone of new zonal complexes of NCB in Lucknow and Dehradun
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States/UTs in New Delhi. On this occasion, the Union Home Minister launched Television Commercials (TVCs) to spread awareness against narcotic substances and laid the foundation stone of new zonal complexes of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) in Lucknow and Dehradun. During the event, the best-performing ANTF of States and UTs were also honoured. In addition, the Union Home Minister launched the newly designed website of the NCB. In the two-day conference organised by the NCB, ANTF heads from 36 States and Union Territories, along with representatives of concerned government departments and other stakeholders, are participating.

In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have for the past five years been taking one step after another in an effort to achieve the difficult goal of a drug free India. He said that the time has now come to deliver a decisive blow against narcotics, which have become the most serious threat to the country and the world, and to achieve victory through collective efforts. Shri Shah said that by 31 December 2029, we will collectively succeed in uprooting the drug trade from India.

Shri Amit Shah said that in the past five years we have achieved success against several challenges such as terrorism in Kashmir, insurgency in the Northeast and the problem of Naxalism. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) with the cooperation of all the states, we have ended these major problems that have confronted the country for decades. He said that the fight against drugs is the most difficult of all battles, but we cannot abandon this fight. Shri Shah said that to build a Viksit Bharat by 2047, to save future generations and to connect the youth with India’s development, the only option before us is to make India drug-free. We will have to fight this problem unitedly and with passion, and we must achieve victory.

Union Home Minister said that the ‘Vision Document 2026-2029’ is like the Gita for all those involved in this fight. This Vision Document has been prepared with great effort after discussions with more than 35 departments. He said that we have prepared the complete roadmap after taking suggestions from all stakeholders, and it has been given to everyone with definite targets. Targets and timelines have also been fixed in it. The Home Minister said that it will also be reviewed after some time. Shri Shah added that the MHA or the NCB cannot do all this alone. We all have to fight this battle with top priority and complete dedication, and we have to win it as well.

Shri Amit Shah said that it should be our shared responsibility and resolve to end this menace of drugs that is hollowing out future generations. Our resolve should be that we will not allow even one gram of drugs to enter the country from anywhere in the world, nor will even one gram of drugs go from our country to the world. He said that we have prepared this roadmap with a resolve for the welfare of youth across the world. Shri Shah said that we will have to work for a drug-free India with sensitivity, with an understanding of its importance, and as the topmost priority. He said – Meet once the parents and siblings of even one young person afflicted by drugs. Until you meet them, intensity in this fight cannot arise in you. A weeping, wailing mother, a younger sister, and a boy who ranked in the top 10 in the Class 10 board examination is slowly moving towards death, while his helpless parents watch. There can be no greater sorrow than this for anyone, and for us too it is a national loss. A talented child who was going to contribute to India’s development in the days to come - his life is ending midway. There can be no greater loss than this for us and for the country.

Union Home Minister said that we have to fight the battle against drugs with clarity. He said that the focal points of this fight have already been identified, and a roadmap has also been prepared at the state level to take intelligence, investigation, financial action and prosecution in one direction. Shri Shah said that in the first ANTF conference we had created an institutional mechanism and strengthened it. In the second ANTF conference, we discussed capability, action and execution in order to convert that mechanism into action. Today, the third ANTF conference will convert this roadmap into a decisive battle.

Shri Amit Shah said that whatever we have done so far is not enough. Until the Principal of every school, the Patwari of the village, the PSI of the police station, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary of the state, and even the Home Secretary of the Government of India, work in one direction, we will not achieve success. He said that today’s conference is the most important because this time we will move forward towards complete victory by fixing Target, Timeline and Accountability.

Union Home Minister said that we now have to move from Meeting to Mission, from Reporting to Result, from Seizure to the dismantling of Networks, and from Case to Conviction. He said that until all departments of the state governments and the Government of India engage in this work, we cannot move forward.

Shri Amit Shah said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has set the target of building a Viksit Bharat by August 15, 2047 before the 140 crore citizens of the country, when India will be at the forefront globally in every sector. He said that if we are to achieve this goal, we cannot do so with a youth power and future generation hollowed out by addiction. He stated that India is the youngest country in the world, which is why the threat is also the largest for us in the global context. This is our necessity because the health, skills, labour, and thinking capacity of the youth alone can lead the country to that goal, and drugs damage all four of these capacities.

Union Home Minister said that for emerging challenges such as synthetic drugs, diversion of precursor chemicals, new communication technologies, dark-net, drug markets, crypto, dead-drop delivery systems, and international drug networks, a team of officers who think 'out-of-the-box' should be constituted in every state, and success should be shared and implemented across the entire nation.

Shri Amit Shah stated that the Vision Document 2026–2029 rests on four pillars: Enforcement, intelligence & operations, Control of precursor & synthetic drugs, Demand & harm reduction, and Capacity building & coordination. Over 100 targets have been categorized across these four pillars. Under the target of registering 1 lakh Nashamukt Mitras outlined in the Vision Document, various ministries have registered 46,780 Nashamukt Mitras so far, and they are already operational. To take this campaign to the grassroots level, Nashamukt Mitras will visit 10 lakh schools, colleges, and institutions across the country in the coming days to caution the youth and sensitize campus directors.

Shri Amit Shah said that today we are discussing converting the roadmap into results, and the most crucial element of the brainstorming taking place over these two days is compassion. Our goal should be to transform the ANTF into an ‘Anti-Narco Mission Command’, and State Chief Secretaries will need to adopt a different approach regarding manpower, technology, budget, and other resources. The Home Minister added that the Government of India is emphasizing technology and forensics in capacity building.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation stated that instead of maintaining a seizure-centric approach, we must move forward with the objective of dismantling entire networks. Our priority, along with backward-forward investigation, must also include financial investigation and tracing digital links. Our strike must hit the funds earned by drug dealers. Shri Shah said that cartels must be targeted at three levels: the entry point, the inter-state distribution system, and the local sales networks within districts. Further, districts will be categorized into three clusters: those where drugs are manufactured or enter the country, those serving as transportation corridors, and those where consumption takes place.

Union Home Minister stated that we must increase the utilization of PITNDPS, as there is a strong need for it in the country. A complete roadmap from investigation to conviction must be formulated in coordination with public prosecutors. A dedicated campaign must be launched to deport foreign accused present in India and blacklist them so they can never re-enter the country. Moreover, the fugitives who are supplying drugs to the country from abroad should be caught and brought before the Indian courts. By targeting borders and production centres, all loopholes must be plugged. Every ANTF should integrate the entire process of converting information to actionable intelligence into the work culture of their respective state police force. The Home Minister expressed confidence that we will succeed in this fight against drugs and emerge victorious.

Participation in this national conference will assist states, departments, and agencies under the 'Whole of Government Approach' to move forward with renewed resolve to effectively combat drug trafficking across the country over the next three years.

The deliberations held during the conference will help strengthen the effective enforcement of drug control laws and make the strategies adopted to protect the country's youth from drugs more impactful. This national event will provide an effective platform to bolster a future-ready partnership between the NCB and ANTFs of States and Union Territories to tackle drug abuse and fulfil the pledge of a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Department of Fertilizers Galvanizes Workforce with Special Creative & Participatory Initiatives Under ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’
Department Focuses on Employee Motivation through 'Kabaad Se Kala' and Idea-Sharing Drives
'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026': Department of Fertilizers Empowers Workforce to Champion Circular Economy
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

To streamline institutional initiatives and maximize on-ground impact during the nationwide "Swachhata Hi Seva" (SHS) Campaign 2026 (being observed from September 17 to October 2, 2026), a comprehensive review and sensitization meeting was convened on September 22, 2026, at 11:00 AM under the chairmanship of the Senior Economic Advisor, Department of Fertilizers (DoF), Government of India, Shri Kuntal Sensarma.

The meeting witnessed wide institutional participation from key stakeholders across the sector, including officers of the Department of Fertilizers, representatives from the Fertilizer Industry Coordination Committee (FICC), and senior management executives, plant heads and designated Swachhata Nodal Officers from all Fertilizer PSUs, Cooperatives, and Joint Venture/Private Fertilizer Companies. The primary objective of the session was to evaluate the impact of the initial kick-off phase launched on September 17 and enforce unified alignment across administrative headquarters, manufacturing plants, and field formations to drive mass public and employee mobilization.

Focus on Five Core Thematic Pillars:

Following directions emerging from high-level inter-ministerial deliberations, the Chair emphasized the disciplined execution of 11 dated activities categorized under five foundational thematic pillars across all units and townships:

  • Swachhata Hi Seva: Intensive, end-to-end cleaning and beautification drives across office premises, workstation cubicles, residential quarters, plants, and adjacent public areas, with special emphasis on sites of cultural, historical, and tourism importance.
  • Kabaad Se Kala (Art from Waste): Creative initiatives encouraging personnel to repurpose office and industrial waste into functional, aesthetic, or artistic installations. Aimed at reducing carbon footprints, reusing resources, and institutionalizing circular-economy principles, departmental staff and PSU units have been invited to submit their innovative entries by September 28, 2026.
  • Khel & Khel Bhawana: Organizing sports meets, fitness challenges, and community games—particularly on holidays—to foster health, discipline, teamwork, and an active lifestyle among employees, their families, and children.
  • Samvad: Hosting interactive seminars, expert discussions, and awareness dialogues centred on water conservation, ecological balance, and sustainable environmental practices to drive institutional and personal behavioural change.
  • Gyan Yatra: Conducting community awareness marches and rallies featuring informative placards to propagate core messages on sanitation, environmental stewardship, and civic responsibility, actively involving youth and local communities.

National Culmination: 'Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath' on October 1:

A critical directive was issued for the national mega-event scheduled for October 1, 2026. All fertilizer PSUs, cooperatives, industrial units, and field offices were instructed to ensure 100% workforce participation for the voluntary cleanliness drive under the national banner “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath”, dedicating one full hour of synchronized Shramdaan across all installations.

Employee Ideation and Periodic Safai Audits:

In line with earlier operational directives, senior officers of the Department are undertaking periodic 'Safai Audits' to inspect sanitation standards and sustain cleanliness benchmarks. To promote participatory governance from the ground up, the Department continues to run the 'Ek Sujaav Swachhata Ki Or' initiative, actively encouraging personnel to submit innovative, practical ideas to enhance workplace hygiene and administrative efficiency.

Real-Time Digital Monitoring & National Reporting:

To guarantee operational transparency and measurable outcomes, all participating entities were directed to upload high-resolution photographic evidence, short video documentation, and performance metrics on a daily basis directly onto the dedicated SHS-2026 Portal. Concurrently, units will maintain real-time reporting via the official institutional WhatsApp network. All uploaded field metrics will flow directly into the centralized repository for National-Level Performance Reporting, with comprehensive consolidated dossiers to be submitted by October 7, 2026.

The Department of Fertilizers reiterates that the sustained success of the Swachhata mission rests upon the dedication and active participation of its personnel, driving a cleaner, greener, and more responsive administrative environment.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Greenery to Prosperity with NSFDC-WBSCDC Support
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

Timely institutional support can help women organise themselves, build sustainable livelihoods and improve the well-being of their families. Whileas limited access to affordable finance often prevents rural women from starting income-generating activities and achieving economic independence.

Maa Lakshmi Mahila Samiti, an 11-member Self-Help Group in Purulia district, West Bengal, transformed its livelihood through greenhouse farming with financial assistance of Rs. 1 lakh under NSFDC's Mahila Samriddhi Yojana. The loan was disbursed through WBSCDC on 5 February 2025.

Before receiving the assistance, the members had no regular source of income and faced financial uncertainty. Despite their willingness to work, limited access to capital prevented them from starting a sustainable livelihood activity.

The members learned about the scheme through the district office of the West Bengal Scheduled Castes Development Corporation. They subsequently applied for financial assistance to undertake greenhouse farming on leased land. The loan provided the capital required to begin cultivation and establish a collective source of livelihood.

Through sustained effort and cooperation, the group successfully developed its greenhouse farming activity. Each member now earns approximately Rs. 4,000 to Rs. 8,000 per month. The additional income has improved the economic condition of their families and enabled them to meet household needs with greater confidence.

Today, the members of Maa Lakshmi Mahila Samiti are moving forward with greater self-confidence and financial independence. Their journey demonstrates how timely credit and institutional support can empower rural women to create sustainable livelihoods. The group has expressed its gratitude to NSFDC and WBSCDC for supporting its journey towards prosperity and self-reliance.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister celebrates World Rhino Day
PM shares initiation of Project Rhino
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today celebrated the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros on the occasion of World Rhino Day and lauded all those at the forefront of its protection. He noted that Assam now holds nearly 80 percent of the world’s rhino population and that Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.

The Prime Minister highlighted that rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal, while the successful reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, is creating history. He stated that this demonstrates the sustained commitment of the people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states. Furthermore, to take species conservation forward in the country, he shared that Project Rhino has been initiated to provide financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement, and understanding population dynamics.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister wrote:

"On World Rhino Day, we celebrate the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros and laud all those at the forefront of its protection.

Assam now holds nearly 80% of the world’s rhino population and Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.

On one hand, rhinos have either returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal. On the other hand, success of reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa (Uttar Pradesh) is creating history. This shows the sustained commitment of our people towards animal protection and active wildlife management in the range states.

Taking species conservation in the country forward, I am happy to share that Project Rhino has been initiated for financial and technical support to the range states for protection, habitat management, genetic improvement and understanding population dynamics."

On World Rhino Day, we celebrate the magnificent greater one-horned rhinoceros and laud all those at the forefront of its protection.

Assam now holds nearly 80% of the world’s rhino population and Kaziranga’s efforts to end rhino poaching have been extensively appreciated.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Signs MoU with SSNNL to Simplify Approval Framework for National Highway and Irrigation Infrastructure Projects in Gujarat
MoU aims to strengthen inter-departmental coordination, facilitate faster approvals and ensure seamless execution of National Highway and Irrigation infrastructure projects
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi

To strengthen inter-agency coordination and expedite infrastructure development, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish a simplified and time-bound framework for granting approvals for National Highway, canal and pipeline crossings across the State of Gujarat. The MoU aims to strengthen inter-departmental coordination, facilitate faster approvals and ensure seamless execution of National Highway and Irrigation infrastructure projects. The MoU was signed by Regional Officer-Gandhinagar, NHAI and Chief Engineer (QC, Tech. & CPC), SSNNL in presence of Directors from SSNNL and other officials at Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

A key feature of the MoU is mutual waiver of various fees, charges and other levies by NHAI and SSNNL for all National Highway, canal and pipeline crossings covered under the agreement. This provision will help in reducing project costs, eliminate avoidable procedural bottlenecks and optimize the utilization of public funds to accelerate the pace of infrastructure development.

The MoU also lays down a framework for early sharing of project information, adoption of standardized engineering practices as well as clearly defined responsibilities for the construction and maintenance of crossing structures. These measures will facilitate better project planning and ensure adherence to high standards of quality and operational efficiency.

The MoU marks a significant milestone in promoting integrated infrastructure planning in Gujarat by fostering closer coordination between NHAI and SSNL. The collaborative framework will accelerate the implementation of both National Highways and irrigation infrastructure projects in Gujarat, while improving efficiency, implementation timelines and reducing overall financial implication associated with project execution.

By enabling faster approvals and strengthening coordination, the MoU reinforces NHAI’s commitment to develop world-class infrastructure that not only enhances connectivity but also supports economic growth.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
9th Molecular Virology Meeting brings together India’s virology community to advance research, translation and preparedness
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi

The 9th Molecular Virology Meeting (MVM 2026) concluded on 18th September 2026 at BRIC–National Institute of Immunology (BRIC–NII), New Delhi, bringing together around 200 clinicians, researchers and students from across India to discuss emerging questions in viral biology and the translation of virology research into vaccines, therapeutics, diagnostics and public-health capabilities.

Initiated in 2009, the Molecular Virology Meeting has grown into an annual forum for the Indian virology community, bringing together researchers working across the continuum from molecular mechanisms of viral infection and host–virus interactions to viral pathogenesis, immunity, evolution and immune evasion, epidemiology, clinical virology and translational research.

The 2026 edition was hosted by BRIC–NII with the support of the International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB) and the Regional Centre for Biotechnology (RCB), providing a platform for researchers across institutions and disciplines to exchange findings, identify emerging research directions and discuss opportunities to strengthen the translation of virology research into technologies and solutions for public health

The two-day meeting opened with a keynote address by Dr. Naveen Kumar, Director, ICMR–National Institute of Virology, Pune, titled “Flip the Switch: Host Factors That Block or Boost Viruses.” The scientific programme brought together research on diverse viral systems, including influenza, dengue, chikungunya, HIV, hepatitis E, West Nile virus, coronaviruses and respiratory syncytial virus, with discussions spanning viral entry and replication, host responses, immune regulation, viral adaptation and molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis.

A significant focus of MVM 2026 was the interface between fundamental virology and translation. The session on Translational Virology: Vaccines & Therapeutics featured work on antiviral therapeutics, antibody discovery and theranostics, alongside studies addressing viral evolution and epidemiology.

The meeting also looked beyond individual research programmes to examine how India can build a stronger national virology innovation and preparedness ecosystem. A panel discussion, “Future of Virology Research and its Contribution in BioE3 Policy: Advancing Towards Viksit Bharat,” brought together representatives from academia, research institutions, and industry. Moderated by Dr Nimesh Gupta (BRIC-NII), the panel brought together Dr Naveen Kumar (ICMR-NIV), Prof Saumitra Das (IISc), Dr Sudhanshu Vrati (RCB), Prof Sanjeev Galande (Shiv Nadar University), and Dr Subeer Mazumdar (Sun Pharma Science Foundation). 

The discussion centred on a fundamental challenge: How can the Indian virology community translate its scientific strengths and capabilities that contribute to the broader vision of BioE3 and Viksit Bharat? Panelists examined the need for a more connected pathway from discovery and validation to scale-up and products, the development of platform technologies for vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics, funding mechanisms that support translation beyond individual projects, stronger academia–industry–government partnerships, and capabilities required for viral disease surveillance and health security. The panel discussion made it clear that virology has a much larger role to play in the vision of Viksit Bharat.

By bringing basic scientists, clinicians, translational researchers, funding agencies and industry perspectives into the same forum, MVM 2026 highlighted the increasingly interconnected nature of modern virology—where understanding viral mechanisms must go hand in hand with the ability to translate that knowledge into preparedness, technologies and solutions for emerging health challenges.

The programme comprised seven scientific sessions, spotlight talks, poster presentations and the panel discussion, followed by an award ceremony and concluding session.

“As a student, being part of MVM 2026 was a valuable learning experience. It was inspiring to hear leading virologists discuss diverse areas of virus biology and also gave us an opportunity to interact with researchers from across the country. Being involved in organising the meeting made the experience even more meaningful, as we got to see first-hand how scientific ideas, discussions and collaborations come together to create a vibrant research community.”—Bhavya Ahuja, PhD Scholar, BRIC-NII

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
European Parliament delegation calls on Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Discussions focus on Effective Implementation of India-EU FTA, Deeper Cooperation in Science, Technology and Emerging Technologies
India-EU Partnership Opens New Avenues for Cooperation in AI, Quantum Technologies, Semiconductors and Advanced Research: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Minister Calls for Stronger India-EU Collaboration on Climate, Clean and Green Technologies and Green Hydrogen
India Seeks Tangible Outcomes from Trade and Technology Council and Greater Research Collaboration through Horizon Europe
Science, Technology and Innovation to Remain Key Pillars of Expanding India-EU Strategic Partnership says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

European Parliament Committee delegation on Industry, Research & Energy (ITRE), led by Angelika Winzig and Austria, Raffaele Stancanelli, today called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh and held a wide range discussion, with focus on effective implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) and deeper cooperation with the European Union in science, technology, research and, critical and emerging technologies.

The Minister said the India-EU strategic partnership offers significant opportunities for closer collaboration in areas of mutual priority, with science and research forming an integral part of the partnership.

The European Parliament delegation comprised Member, ITRE; Angelika Winzig, MEP, Austria, Raffaele Stancanelli, MEP, and Full Member, ITRE; Mohammed Chahim, MEP, Netherlands, S&D Vice-President and Full Member, ITRE; Raúl de la Hoz Quintano, MEP, Spain and Full Member, ITRE; Nicolás González Casares, MEP, Spain and Full Member, ITRE; Morten Løkkegaard, MEP, Denmark and Full Member, ITRE; Jüri Ratas, MEP, Estonia and Full Member, ITRE; and Virginijus Sinkevičius, MEP, Lithuania and Full Member, ITRE.

The Indian side, led by Minister Dr Jitendra Singh, comprised Dr. Rajiv Jaiswal, Department of Space; Dr. Nisha Mendiratta and Dr. Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Department of Science & Technology; Dr. Dhananjay Tiwary, Department of Biotechnology; Dr. Prabhasis Bandyopadhyay, CSIR; Dr. Anil Chauhan, Department of Atomic Energy; Dr. Ekta Kapoor, Department of Science & Technology; and Ms. Nidhi Choudhary, Ministry of External Affairs.

Speaking on behalf of the delegation, Angelika Winzig, MEP from Austria and Full Member of ITRE, thanked the Minister for the meeting and said that India is a key strategic partner for the European Union. She said the delegation’s visit was aimed at gaining a deeper understanding of India’s industrial and technology policies and identifying areas for closer cooperation. She referred to shared interests in strengthening industrial competitiveness, ensuring secure and resilient critical supply chains, and advancing the green and digital transitions, while welcoming continued dialogue between India and the European Parliament on these issues.

During the discussions, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the early and effective implementation of the India-EU FTA should remain a collective priority and expressed India’s expectation of continued support from the European Parliament for its early signing and ratification. He said the FTA would open new opportunities for businesses, consumers and skilled professionals and provide further momentum to the multifaceted India-EU strategic partnership.

On India’s research and innovation priorities, the Minister said research and innovation are central to the Government’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with greater focus on high-impact research, translation of research into technologies and products, and increased industry participation. He referred to the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) and the EUR 10 billion Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) initiative, aimed at catalysing high-risk, high-impact research and nurturing deep-tech startups.

Dr. Jitendra Singh invited greater India-EU cooperation in frontier and emerging areas including Artificial Intelligence, quantum technologies, advanced materials, biotechnology and semiconductors, besides high-performance computing and next-generation telecommunications, including 6G. He said quantum technologies offer significant scope for cooperation across research, applications, skills and development of the wider quantum ecosystem. In AI, India is particularly interested in applications in areas such as healthcare and science, while ensuring responsible and trustworthy adoption.

On semiconductors, the Minister said India’s growing semiconductor and electronics ecosystem and the EU’s efforts towards resilient and secure semiconductor supply chains provide scope for greater cooperation. He said synergies could be explored between India’s semiconductor initiatives and the EU Chips framework in areas including research, innovation, investment and ecosystem development.

The Minister also called for stronger collaboration on clean and green technologies, climate and environmental challenges, identifying these as important areas for research cooperation. Under the India-EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC), substantial progress has been made on priority clean and green technology workstreams, including a EUR 60 million joint investment over four years to support collaborative research on waste-to-hydrogen, marine pollution and recycling of electric vehicle batteries.

The discussions also covered the proposed India-EU Innovation Hub on Electric Vehicle Charging Technologies and Testing, which is being developed as a platform bringing together research capacity, testing infrastructure, standards expertise and startup ecosystems from both sides. India and the EU are also sharing knowledge on Hydrogen Valleys and working towards cooperation on hydrogen-related safety standards. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the potential of cooperation in green hydrogen could also support greater trade and investment, including green hydrogen exports from India to the EU over the medium term.

On the Horizon Europe programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s association would expand opportunities for Indian researchers to partner with European institutions in cutting-edge research areas of mutual priority. He said discussions on India’s association are progressing well, with substantial convergence, while some legal, financial and institutional issues remain under discussion. India remains committed to concluding the negotiations expeditiously and looks forward to an arrangement that is balanced, mutually beneficial and expands opportunities for researchers, institutions and industry.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also invited the ITRE delegation to identify areas where Indian and European research and innovation priorities can converge, particularly where collaboration can lead to joint research, technology development and scale-up. He said India sees Europe as a significant research partner given its strong research institutions, advanced research infrastructure and innovation ecosystem.

The meeting covered India’s research priorities, critical and emerging technologies, implementation and follow-up of the India-EU Trade and Technology Council, and the state of play on India’s association with Horizon Europe, reinforcing the scope for further engagement across science, technology, innovation and clean technologies.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Preventive Health Check-up Camp Organised at National Media Centre under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Camp organised for Officers/Officials and Safai Mitras of PIB, Delhi
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, a Preventive Health Check-up and Consultation Camp was organised today for the Officers/Officials and Safai Mitras (Housekeeping Staff) of the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Delhi, at the National Media Centre, New Delhi.

The health camp was organised in association with Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital, New Delhi. A team of doctors from RML Hospital provided health check-up and medical consultation to the Officers/Officials and Safai Mitras attending the camp.

The initiative aimed at promoting preventive healthcare and general well-being among the personnel of PIB, with special focus on the health and welfare of Safai Mitras. The participants were provided an opportunity to undergo health assessment and seek medical advice from the medical team.

The health camp forms part of the activities being undertaken under the ‘SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivirs’ component of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, which emphasises the welfare and well-being of sanitation workers through preventive health check-ups and other support measures.

Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 is being jointly organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. The campaign seeks to strengthen collective participation and volunteerism towards cleanliness and reinforce the spirit of a Swachh Bharat.

The organisation of the preventive health check-up camp at the National Media Centre reflects PIB’s commitment towards promoting a clean, healthy and supportive workplace and ensuring the well-being and dignity of Safai Mitras who contribute significantly to maintaining cleanliness and hygiene in the workplace.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Substance Dependence to Sporting Ambition: J&K’s Sajjad's Journey of Recovery and Reintegration
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi

Timely treatment, counselling and rehabilitation can help affected individuals regain their health, rebuild confidence and return to productive community life. Otherwise substance dependence can interrupt education, employment, family relationships and personal aspirations.

Sajjad (name changed), a 25-year-old graduate, full-time employee and talented regional cricketer from Central Kashmir’s Budgam district in Jammu and Kashmir, overcame substance dependence with support from CHAARAH SAAZ, a District De-Addiction Centre supported under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction. He has resumed sporting activities and now motivates other young people through the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

Substance dependence had significantly affected Sajjad's physical health, emotional well-being and sporting career. It led to a loss of confidence, social isolation and disruption of his athletic aspirations. His family faced severe financial hardship, emotional stress and social stigma as they witnessed his condition deteriorate, making access to quality treatment and rehabilitation difficult.

Despite these challenges, Sajjad remained determined to overcome substance dependence, support his family and return to cricket. He also aspired to acquire technical skills, rebuild a meaningful future and encourage others to stay away from substance use.

Through NAPDDR-supported services at CHAARAH SAAZ, DDAC Budgam, Sajjad received free medical detoxification and treatment, medical supervision, individual and family counselling, psychological care and nutritional support. His rehabilitation also included fitness and yoga sessions, computer and digital literacy training, skill development, sports reintegration support, livelihood guidance and regular follow-up interventions.

The comprehensive intervention helped Sajjad regain his physical health, strengthen his emotional resilience and restore his confidence. With sustained treatment and support, he successfully reintegrated into society and resumed his sporting activities.

Today, Sajjad actively participates in counselling and peer-support sessions and serves as a campaigner for the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. By sharing his recovery journey, he has emerged as a role model who inspires other young people to seek help, pursue recovery and choose a healthy, purposeful and drug-free life.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
IAF'S JOINT AIR DEFENCE EXERCISE WITH JAPAN ‘EXERCISE VEER GUARDIAN 2026' CONCLUDES
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

The bilateral air exercise ‘Veer Guardian 2026' between the Indian Air Force (IAF) and Japan Air Self Defense Force (JASDF) concluded at Air Force Station Jodhpur on 22 September 2026. The exercise served as a vital platform for enhancing interoperability and strengthening the strategic partnership between the two Air Forces. The IAF deployed a mix of aircraft, including Su-30 MKI, Rafale, and indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas. The JASDF participated with the F-2A fighter aircraft.

During the joint training spanning 14 days, IAF and JASDF engaged in wide range of advanced flying missions encompassing within visual range combat and coordinated multi - aircraft missions. On Distinguished Visitor's Day, General Takehiro Morita, Chief of Staff, JASDF and Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff visited Air Force Station Jodhpur and flew the indigenous Tejas fighter aircraft.

The exercise also witnessed numerous ground interactions between IAF and JASDF personnel such as Subject Matter Expert Exchanges, operational discussions, missions planning conferences, engineering interactions, maintenance practice and aerospace safety briefings wherein various aspects were discussed by both the sides. This enabled the participating contingents to obtain an invaluable insight into each other's best practices and learn from each other's unique capabilities.

Exercise Veer Guardian 26 concludes as a testament to the enduring friendship and professional camaraderie between the two Air Forces. This engagement continues to pave the way for enhanced collaboration and strategic depth of the defence partnership between India and Japan.

***

JS/VK/SM

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam
Vice-President calls for judicious use, conservation and integrated management of water resources
“Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha”: Vice-President
Bharat's traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges: Vice President
Small water-saving actions can serve the interest of humanity and the world: Vice-President
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 2:40PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The five-day event, being organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti from September 22 to 26, is centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.”

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the 9th India International Water Week 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centred on the theme “Climate Resilient Water Management.”

Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, MoS Shri V. Somanna & Shri Raj Bhushan… pic.twitter.com/ELgtxDQVnE

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) September 22, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that water is the foundation of life and civilisations, stressing the need for its judicious use, conservation and effective management.

Recalling his childhood experiences in Tamil Nadu, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that he had personally witnessed water scarcity and remembered the importance attached to bringing potable water to people. “Saving water is of paramount importance for humanity and the globe,” he said.

The Vice-President recalled that more than two decades ago, he undertook a 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, one of the objectives of which was to create awareness about river interlinking, water conservation and proper management of water resources. He said river interlinking could help address situations where some regions face floods while others experience drought.

Emphasising India’s civilisational connect with rivers, the Vice-President said Indian communities had developed rich traditions and practices for conserving, sharing and managing water over centuries. “Our traditional wisdom provides valuable lessons for addressing today’s water challenges,” he said.

The Vice-President noted that India accounts for about 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area and 18 per cent of its population, while possessing only about 4 per cent of global freshwater resources. He stressed that India’s water-use requirements cannot be compared with those of countries having greater water availability and smaller populations.

Calling for behavioural change, he urged citizens to adopt simple water-saving practices in their daily lives. “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours. We can close the tap while brushing our teeth. These may appear to be small things, but within these small actions lies the interest of humanity and the world,” he said.

The Vice-President said climate change, rapid urbanisation and population growth were making water management increasingly complex. He stressed the need for an integrated approach encompassing river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation.

The Vice-President highlighted the importance of cooperation among States in addressing water-sharing issues. Appreciating the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he noted that 10 inter-State MoUs have been signed for water sharing.He appreciated the efforts of the Union Government, the Ministry of Jal Shakti and participating States in promoting cooperative solutions.He particularly highlighted the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as an important example of inter-State cooperation.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that as India moves towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, efficient and sustainable water management will be critical. He recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged citizens to make water conservation a mass movement.

He emphasised the need for greater water-use efficiency, recycling and reuse, particularly in view of the substantial demand for water from agriculture and the growing requirements of industry.He called for a shift from reactive to predictive and technology-enabled water management.

Calling for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said water challenges cannot be addressed by any single institution, sector or State.He expressed confidence that the deliberations at India International Water Week-2026 would generate innovative technological, policy, socio-economic and environmental approaches for climate-resilient and integrated water management.

Urging all participants to share knowledge, build partnerships and commit themselves to saving and conserving water, the Vice-President said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.”

On the occasion, the Vice-President launched the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework and AI/ML-driven Integrated Reservoir Sediment Management, marking important steps towards technology-enabled and climate-resilient water management.

Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil, Ministers of State for Jal Shakti Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Secretaries of the Ministry of Jal Shakti Smt. Archana Varma and Shri Ashok Meena, Chairman, Central Water Commission, Shri Anupam Prasad, and delegates and experts from India and abroad were present on the occasion.


***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
7th High-Level Meeting of the OPEC-India Energy Dialogue
The Seventh High-Level Meeting of the OPEC-India Energy Dialogue was held on 22nd September 2026 in New Delhi, India
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 2:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Meeting was co-chaired by HE Hardeep Singh Puri, India’s Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and HE Haitham Al Ghais, OPEC Secretary General.

Discussions focused on oil market stability, energy security and the importance of adequate and timely investment across the oil industry. Both parties reviewed the short-, medium- and long-term outlooks, underscoring India's crucial role in global economic expansion and energy demand growth.

In his remarks, HE Hardeep Singh Puri underlined that India and OPEC share a naturally complementary and mutually beneficial relationship and thanked Secretary General for his contribution in strengthening this partnership. He emphasized that India values its longstanding engagement with OPEC and its Member Countries, which has contributed significantly to mutual understanding and cooperation on key energy issues.

He noted that “As one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies, India will remain an important driver of global energy demand in the decades ahead. A sustained dialogue between producers and consumers is essential to support investment, strengthen energy resilience and ensure reliable energy supplies for global growth and development.”

Appreciating OPEC's efforts towards promoting stability and transparency in global energy markets during a period marked by geopolitical uncertainties and market volatility, he called on OPEC and India to work closely in advancing a balanced, stable and predictable global energy market.

In his remarks, HE Al Ghais stated that “Dialogue with India is a priority for OPEC because we recognize India’s importance within the current global energy landscape and the fact that this importance will only increase in the decades ahead”. He added that the “OPEC-India Energy Dialogue is eleven years strong, having been launched in New Delhi in 2015”.

The Secretary General commended India’s balanced, realistic and pragmatic approach to addressing energy challenges, emphasizing that “many of India’s energy priorities are OPEC’s priorities”.

HE Al Ghais also praised the Indian Government's firm commitment to international collaboration and dialogue. He stressed, “What is particularly heartening about our dialogue is the fact that the Indian Government has consistently advocated diplomacy and dialogue as the means of resolving the great challenges of our age”.

HE Al Ghais thanked all participants for their valuable contributions. He also expressed the OPEC Secretariat’s sincere gratitude to HE Hardeep Singh Puri for the gracious hospitality extended to the OPEC delegation.

The Meeting commended the progress achieved to date within the framework of the dialogue, including at the technical level. It concluded with both parties underscoring the vital importance of fostering even deeper energy cooperation between OPEC and India.

It was agreed to hold the 8th High-Level Meeting of the OPEC-India Energy Dialogue at a mutually convenient date in Vienna, Austria.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Department of Food and Public Distribution starts ‘Swachhata Hi Seva-2026’ campaign
Campaign focuses on behavioural and cultural transformation under the theme ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, along with its Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), attached and subordinate offices, has commenced the ‘Swachhata Hi Seva-2026’ campaign across the country. The campaign is being undertaken in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Urban Development and the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, with a focus on cleanliness and sanitation.

The campaign, being observed under the theme ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’, seeks to promote behavioural and cultural transformation and encourage greater participation of citizens and stakeholders in cleanliness initiatives.

Swachhata Pledge and cleanliness drive

Shri Sanjeev Chopra, Secretary, Department of Food and Public Distribution, administered the Swachhata pledge to officials of the Department on 17 September 2026 at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. The pledge was followed by a cleanliness drive in the premises.

On 18 September 2026, officials of DFPD participated in a slogan competition on Swachhata. The Department also organised a workshop for Safai Mitras, focusing on their wellbeing, health and social security, which constitute one of the six pillars of the Swachhata Hi Seva-2026 campaign. During the workshop, Safai Mitras were informed about the activities planned for them during the campaign and various social welfare schemes of the Government of India and the benefits available under these schemes.

Activities undertaken by PSUs and attached offices

The Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) organised a cleanliness and beautification drive at Mayur Vihar, Delhi, on 19 and 20 September 2026. A painting competition was also organised at Veer Chand Singh Garhwali Sarvodaya Bal Vidyalaya on 18 September 2026.

The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute (IGMRI) and its field stations undertook several activities as part of the campaign. IGMRI Field Station, Ludhiana, administered the Swachhata pledge followed by a cleanliness drive on the campus on 17 September 2026. IGMRI Field Station, Hyderabad, organised an art competition at a nearby Government school, with prizes distributed to selected students.

A Jal Sanchay Samvad was also conducted by officials of IGMRI Hyderabad. An awareness programme and cleanliness drive were further organised by IGMRI Ludhiana.

The Food Corporation of India (FCI) commenced the campaign on 17 September 2026 across its Headquarters, Regional and District Offices and depots with the administration of the Swachhata pledge and display of campaign banners.

HEADQUARTERS

Regional Office Maharashtra and Odisha

Regional Office Gujarat and Amravati:

As part of the campaign, a comprehensive health check-up camp was organised on 18 September 2026 at FCI Headquarters, New Delhi, and various FCI offices and depots for Safai Mitras and their families..

HEADQUARTERS

Medical Camp organized at Regional Office HARYANA and Bhopal.

RO ODISHA and NEF

DO DHARMSHALA and RO TELANGANA

 

The Quality Control Cell (QCC) offices organised oath-taking ceremonies, banner displays and weekly cleanliness pledges on 17 September 2026 under Pillar-2: ‘Swachh Paathshala – Yuva for Swachhata’.

Staff and public sensitisation and awareness activities were also organised by the QCC offices on 18 September 2026

QCC Bhubaneswar

               QCC Lucknow

The National Sugar Institute (NSI), Kanpur, also actively participated in the campaign. The Director, NSI, administered the Swachhata pledge to officials of the Institute on 17 September 2026.

 

Through these initiatives, DFPD and its PSUs, attached and subordinate offices are reinforcing the message of cleanliness, sanitation and collective responsibility, while encouraging participation of employees, Safai Mitras, students and the wider community in the Swachhata Hi Seva-2026 campaign.

The Department will continue to undertake cleanliness, awareness, sensitisation and community participation activities during the campaign period, with emphasis on sustainable cleanliness practices and the dignity, health and wellbeing of sanitation workers. The collective efforts are aimed at strengthening a culture of cleanliness and contributing to the vision of a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

***

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Progressing Towards Universal Health Coverage
Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
Posted On: 22 SEP 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi

Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri-Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) serves as the flagship financial protection pillar of India’s healthcare system, providing annual cashless hospitalisation coverage of upto Rs.5 lakh per family to economically vulnerable citizens. Marking its eighth anniversary, the scheme now covers about 33% of India's population with Ayushman cards, having funded 13.25 crore admissions worth Rs. 2.03 lakh crore and drastically reducing out-of-pocket medical expenses. This inpatient care model works alongside three complementary pillars-Ayushman Arogya Mandirs for primary care, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission for integrated health IDs, and PM-ABHIM for physical infrastructure-to achieve comprehensive universal health coverage across the nation.

Ensuring Health Coverage for All

Investing in healthcare makes communities more resilient, capable, and productive. Universal health coverage is about ensuring everyone, including the most vulnerable families, gets access to affordable, quality healthcare, enabling them to live healthy and fulfilling lives.

The Government of India launched the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan-Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) eight years ago on September 23, 2018, to achieve universal health coverage. It is a public health assurance scheme and covers secondary and tertiary care. It is one of the world’s largest public healthcare schemes, with about 33% of India's population  (over 48.51 crore people) already holding Ayushman cards on the scheme’s eighth launch anniversary (as of September 21, 2026).

AB-PMJAY has served people with treatment worth upto Rs. 2.03 lakh crore  in about 13.25 crore hospital admissions through a network of over 38,000 empanelled public and private hospitals (as on August 31, 2026).

AB-PMJAY is one scheme under Ayushman Bharat that is promoting universal health coverage. The other schemes that are building India’s public health infrastructure are: Ayushman Aarogya Mandirs (AAM), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and PM-Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM). Led by AB-PMJAY, these four flagship schemes are strengthening India’s public health infrastructure to deliver universal health coverage.

AB PM-JAY: Saving Citizens from Medical Debt

AB PM-JAY aims to save families from catastrophic medical bills. It provides cashless healthcare services for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties.

In March 2024, the government had also expanded the scheme to include about 37 lakh families of Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), anganwadi workers, and anganwadi helpers.  As on 21.09.26,  more than  44.81 lakh Ayushman cards have been created for ASHAs/AWWs/AWHs under the scheme.

Following this, on September 11, 2024, the Government expanded the scheme to include all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, covering about 6 crore senior citizens.  As on 21.09.26,  more than 1.36 crore senior citizens have Ayushman Vay Vandana cards.

Empowering Vulnerable Beneficiaries

Beneficiary families are identified based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011, using defined deprivation and occupational criteria. The scheme also includes families previously covered under the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY).

  1. Rural Beneficiaries

For rural areas, eligibility under AB PM-JAY is determined based on the deprivation criteria specified in the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC), 2011. Eligible households include those falling under one or more of the following six criteria:

  • D1: Households having only one room with kucha walls and kucha roof;
  • D2: Households having no adult member between 16 and 59 years of age;
  • D3: Female-headed households having no adult male member between 16 and 59 years of age;
  • D4: Households having a disabled member and no able-bodied adult member;
  • D5: Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe households; and
  • D7: Landless households deriving a major part of their income from manual casual labour

2. Urban Beneficiaries

For urban areas, the following 11 occupational categories of workers are eligible for the scheme:

  • Ragpicker
  • Beggar
  • Domestic worker
  • Street vendor/ Cobbler/hawker / other service provider working on streets
  • Construction worker/ Plumber/ Mason/ Labour/ Painter/ Welder/ Security guard/ Coolie and other head-load worker
  • Sweeper/ Sanitation worker/ Mali
  • Home-based worker/ Artisan/ Handicrafts worker/ Tailor
  • Transport worker/ Driver/ Conductor/ Helper to drivers and conductors/ Cart puller/ Rickshaw puller
  • Shop worker/ Assistant/ Peon in small establishment/ Helper/Delivery assistant / Attendant/ Waiter
  • Electrician/ Mechanic/ Assembler/ Repair worker
  • Washer-man/ Chowkidar

3. Additional beneficiary categories covered through specific initiatives

  • Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) and their dependants;
  • Road accident victims covered under PM-RAHAT;
  • Transgender persons covered under the Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) initiative;
  • Eligible children under the PM CARES for Children Scheme who lost both parents, a surviving parent, a legal guardian, or adoptive parents due to the COVID-19 pandemic;
  • Waste pickers and identified sanitation workers covered under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme; and
  • Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) covered under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN).

Aiding the Ailing Elderly

Birmati, a 65-year-old woman from Haryana’s Jind district, suffered a severe fracture in her femoral neck, which connects the hip to the leg. Fortunately for her, she was able to get timely surgery and proper care worth Rs. 44,140 at a district orthopaedic and maternity hospital through the Ayushman Bharat scheme for free. The scheme has proven to be a lifeline for the economically and socially weaker sections of society, providing them with affordable, timely, quality, and accessible healthcare.

AB-PMJAY Funding Structure and Central Budgeting

AB-PMJAY is a centrally sponsored scheme. The sharing of funds between the Centre and the States is in the ratio of 60:40 for all States, except the North-Eastern States, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, and the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, where the sharing ratio is 90:10. For Union Territories without a legislature, the Central Government provides 100% funding, while for Union Territories with a legislature, the Centre and the UT share the funding in the ratio of 60:40. The Union budget estimates have increased over the past few years, with a budget of Rs. 9,500 crore estimated for 2026-27.

 

Reducing Out-of-Pocket Health Expenditure

People are spending much less of their own money on healthcare than they used to. Government data reflects that personal health expenses have also dropped due to higher government funding and free and low-cost schemes like AB-PMJAY.

Apart from AB-PMJAY, Ayushman Bharat’s other schemes are also ensuring that people get universal health coverage.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs: Strengthening Grassroots Primary Care

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAM), the second pillar of Ayushman Bharat, make primary healthcare more accessible to people.  

AAMs are community healthcare centres with medical professionals leading the frontline workers. AAMs are often upgraded from existing health centres that previously provided basic maternal and childcare services or other services.

AAMs are equipped with all the required resources, including:

  • Upgraded infrastructure
  • Additional human resources
  • Essential drugs and diagnostics
  • IT systems, etc.

AAMs go beyond maternal and child health care services. They also provide the following services: Screening and management of diseases, oral, eye, and ear-nose-throat care, and mental health support. First-level emergency and trauma care, and free essential medicines and diagnostics are also provided at these centres.

Since the Government is also expanding AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy) care, there are now AYUSH AAMs for people, too.

AAMs are centres for community health outreach for Community Health Workers and Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs). At these centres, they spread awareness of health programmes, check in on patients, and keep track of community health.

AAMs are also where citizens can connect to healthcare professionals at district, state, or national hospitals through e-Sanjeevani, which is a government-run telemedicine service.

  • More than 50 crore teleconsultations were conducted, including at the AAMs (as of September 17, 2026).

The AAMs have recorded a cumulative footfall of over 540 crores as on date. The government is rapidly building this infrastructure.

Building Digital Health Infrastructure via ABDM   

While a brick-and-mortar infrastructure forms the backbone of universal healthcare delivery, an equally robust digital public infrastructure is also essential. It helps in making healthcare delivery more seamless, efficient, and accessible. Recognising this, the Government of India launched the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in September 2021 to develop an integrated, citizen-centric national digital health ecosystem.

ABDM’s infrastructure rests on the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHAs), which are digital health IDs, similar to the Aadhaar number, for every individual. People’s health records and insurance claims are integrated with the ABHA IDs. Through the ABHA IDs, individuals can connect to insurers, healthcare facilities, doctors, and other services with all their medical history intact through this one interoperable network.

As of 17 September, 2026, over 97.61 crore ABHA IDs are now operational, and over 119.95 crore health records have been linked to the accounts. Women make up 49.74% of the ABHA ID users, men 50.26%, and other genders 0.01% (as on Sept. 17, 2026). Additionally, there are over 5.78 lakh verified healthcare facilities and over 11 lakh healthcare professionals registered on the platform.

Beyond the ABHA, ABDM is a full-fledged digital health ecosystem. It brings all healthcare providers onto one single network.

  • Healthcare Professionals Registry: A national registry of all healthcare professionals-from doctors to AYUSH practitioners - verified and digitally connected.
  • Health Facility Registry: A national registry of health facilities-hospitals, clinics, labs, pharmacies-public and private, all in one place.
  • Unified Health Interface: An open network for health services-like UPI for healthcare. Book appointments, consult doctors, and discover services across any app.
  • Aarogya Setu 2.0: It serves as a unified app to digital health services and Personal Health Record (PHR), accelerating nationwide adoption of digital health.

PM-ABHIM: Bolstering Critical Care and Disease Surveillance

During COVID-19, the government responded swiftly through a unified, whole-of-government approach. Demonstrating a proactive commitment to transforming the national healthcare landscape across local clinics and major hospitals, the government launched the landmark PM-Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) on October 25, 2021, as part of Budget 2021-22.

With a monumental budget of Rs. 64,180 crore (2021-2026), PM-ABHIM focuses on strengthening health infrastructure, bolstering disease surveillance, and expanding health research across urban and rural areas. This effort empowers India to achieve self-reliance and complete resilience in handling future health challenges.

PM-ABHIM focuses on:

  • supporting 23,224 rural health and wellness centres in 10 high-focus states.
  • establishing 13,736 urban health and wellness centres in all states.
  • setting up 3,389 block public health units in 11 high-focus states.
  • setting up 744 integrated public health labs in all districts.
  • establishing 631 critical care hospital blocks in all districts with a population of more than 5 lakh.

Path to Universal Healthcare Coverage        

AB-PMJAY expands access to quality and affordable secondary and tertiary healthcare for eligible beneficiaries, while Ayushman Aarogya Mandirs bring comprehensive primary healthcare closer to communities. ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) enables individuals to create a unique digital health identity and access their health records across participating healthcare facilities. PM-ABHIM strengthens the health system’s infrastructure and preparedness by supporting the development of health centres, laboratories, and critical care facilities from the grassroots to the district level.

Overall, these initiatives strengthen the continuum of healthcare, from primary care and digital health services to hospital-based treatment and resilient health infrastructure, advancing the goal of universal health coverage.
