item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy interacts with EV beneficiaries and distributors from across the country.Highlights India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility
Minister Calls for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility,Emphasises localisation, innovation, cost competitiveness and global capabilities.
Beneficiaries expressed confidence on government policies for e mobility.
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 11:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Heavy Industries & Steel Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy today interacted with beneficiaries and distributors of electric vehicles (EVs) from across the country at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The interaction was organised by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to provide a platform for EV beneficiaries, distributors and industry stakeholders to share their experiences, perspectives and insights on the adoption and use of electric vehicles.

The interaction was attended by Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; senior officials of the Ministry; representatives of the automobile industry; EV manufacturers, distributors and dealers; and EV beneficiaries from different parts of the country. Industry representatives included Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA).

The programme highlighted the growing electric mobility ecosystem in the country and the Government’s sustained efforts towards promoting clean, sustainable and self-reliant transportation.Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, in his Welcome and Opening Remarks, highlighted the Government’s strong policy push for electric mobility and emphasised that localisation is key to building a resilient and self-reliant automotive ecosystem. He noted that initiatives such as PM E-DRIVE and PLI-Auto are supporting domestic manufacturing of critical EV components.

 

Government committed to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047

Addressing the gathering, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy highlighted India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility. He extended his greetings to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday and acknowledged his continued service to the nation.

The Union Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to building an Atmanirbhar Bharat and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy appreciated the leadership and vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in driving India’s transition towards electric mobility and building a cleaner, greener and self-reliant transportation ecosystem. He also appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Heavy Industries in implementing various initiatives and schemes aimed at accelerating EV adoption, strengthening domestic manufacturing and creating an enabling ecosystem for electric mobility.

Highlighting the Government’s comprehensive approach to electric mobility, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy spoke about the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, which supports EV adoption and charging infrastructure, as well as the PLI-Auto and PLI-ACC schemes, which are strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced automotive technologies and battery cells.

The Union Minister emphasised the need for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility, supported by robust manufacturing, innovation and a strong ecosystem. He congratulated EV users for contributing to cleaner mobility and reduced crude oil imports and appreciated the industry’s efforts towards producing world-class vehicles with increasing local content.

He called upon all stakeholders to work together to build a seamless, accessible and globally competitive electric mobility ecosystem aligned with India’s national mission.

The Union Minister further emphasised the importance of listening to the experiences of EV users and other stakeholders on the ground. He noted that feedback from beneficiaries and distributors would help in further strengthening policy implementation and addressing emerging requirements across different segments of the electric mobility ecosystem.

Industry representatives share perspectives on evolving EV landscape

The programme was also addressed by key representatives from the automobile industry. Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA) shared their perspectives on the evolving electric mobility landscape and the industry’s experience with the growing adoption of electric vehicles.

EV beneficiaries share ground-level experiences

At the interaction, EV beneficiaries from across India presented diverse perspectives on the use of electric vehicles across different segments of electric mobility.They spoke about how an electric two-wheeler is supporting his daily mobility and livelihood while providing lower running costs.Ms. Sunita Chaudhary, an e-3W driver, spoke about using an electric three-wheeler for her livelihood and the benefits of lower running costs and reduced driving fatigue.They discussed the suitability of electric four-wheelers for everyday passenger mobility and cleaner transportation.The beneficiaries’ perspectives provided valuable ground-level insights into the benefits of electric mobility across personal mobility, livelihoods, public transport and freight movement. They also expressed confidence in continued Government support and enabling policies to further strengthen India’s electric mobility ecosystem and advance a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future

Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, highlighted India’s rapid progress in electric mobility and said, “Electric mobility is a great opportunity for India to become a global electric mobility player.”

He highlighted key initiatives including FAME I & II, PLI Auto, PLI-ACC, PM E-DRIVE, PM-eBus Sewa (PSM) and the Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Scheme, and called upon industry to focus on cost competitiveness, technology and global capabilities.

The programme reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to advancing India’s Net Zero goals, promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat, strengthening domestic manufacturing and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 through the development of a robust, sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility ecosystem.

The interaction marked an important step towards strengthening dialogue among Government, industry, distributors and EV users and further consolidating India’s journey towards clean, sustainable and globally competitive electric mobility.

***

TPJ

(Release ID: 2311747)

item.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026; Unveils India’s Ambitious Roadmap for Transition to Semicon 2.0, with Expanded Support for Design, Manufacturing, Packaging, R&D and Talent Development
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
item.description: Ministry of Electronics & IT Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026; Unveils India’s Ambitious Roadmap for Transition to Semicon 2.0, with Expanded Support for Design, Manufacturing, Packaging, R&D and Talent Development PM Interacts with Young Chip Designers and Students; Encourages Them to Drive India’s Semiconductor Future PM Calls upon Global Industry to Partner in Building a Complete Semiconductor Ecosystem in India PM Launches New Commercial Semiconductor Production Lines: India Moves from Policy to Production Posted On: 17 SEP 2026…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026; Unveils India’s Ambitious Roadmap for Transition to Semicon 2.0, with Expanded Support for Design, Manufacturing, Packaging, R&D and Talent Development
PM Interacts with Young Chip Designers and Students; Encourages Them to Drive India’s Semiconductor Future
PM Calls upon Global Industry to Partner in Building a Complete Semiconductor Ecosystem in India
PM Launches New Commercial Semiconductor Production Lines: India Moves from Policy to Production
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:36PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 to be held from 17-19 September 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion and highlighting the significance of the event's fifth edition, the Prime Minister extended warm greetings to all participants. He expressed gratitude to the international attendees who had traveled to India to participate in the summit.

Hosted at Yashobhoomi, SEMICON India 2026 features over 600 exhibitors, including approximately 300 international participants, six country pavilions and twelve Indian state pavilions. It also includes a Startup Pavilion and a Workforce Development Zone. On first day, there were about 12,000 visitors at the event.

Shri Ajit Manocha, President & CEO, SEMI, said the global semiconductor market is forecast to reach USD 3 trillion by 2035 and urged India to build indispensable capabilities across key value-chain segments.

Shri Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO, Micron Technology, said commercial DRAM and NAND production is live at Sanand, Gujarat.

Mr. Jochen Hanebeck, CEO, Infineon Technologies, highlighted the company's 2,800+ employees in India, its skilling partnership with NIELIT and opportunities in power semiconductors, smart mobility and automotive electrification.

Dr. Randhir Thakur, CEO & MD, Tata Electronics, confirmed that the construction of Dholera 300mm fab and Jagiroad OSAT facility is on track. He informed that Tata Electronics shall be signing 7 MoUs in the areas including inter-alia semiconductor wafer manufacturing, assembly and test; building advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities; supply of photoresists and advanced chemicals for fab; localization of critical semiconductor materials, and talent development, with Fujifilm, Nexperia, BESI Singapore Pte. Ltd, JSR Corporation etc.

Mr. Toshiki Kawai, CEO, Tokyo Electron, committed support for India's upcoming wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities and announced a semiconductor training centre in Gujarat next year in partnership with the Government of Japan.

Mr. Benjamin Hein, CEO Electronics, Merck, emphasized that fab viability requires parallel local investment in ultra-pure semiconductor chemicals and gases, safe materials handling and certified domestic suppliers.

Dr. Prabu Raja, President, SPG, Applied Materials, announced 'India Vision 2035': a USD 5 billion investment over the next decade and tenfold expansion of its India-based supply-chain capacity by 2035.

Shri Shesha Varadarajan, COO, Lam Research, announced approximately ₹10,000 crore for the company's first silicon-component manufacturing and vertical ingot-processing plant in India, and said its Semiverse programme has reached over 99 universities.

Mr. Wayne Allan, EVP, ASML, reiterated its partnership with Tata Electronics for lithography solutions at the Dholera fab and said ASML is considering the possibility of integrating Indian suppliers for its global supply chain.

Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics & IT, Railways, and I&B noted that while foundational groundwork has been done under Semicon 1.0, including 70,000 design engineers trained and EDA tools deployed across 500+ organizations, Semicon 2.0 scales ecosystem development across six comprehensive pillars: Design, Equipment & Materials, Fabs, Advanced Packaging, Applied R&D and Talent. 

The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with 20 students from academic institutions across the country who presented a memento of 20 chips, designed, fabricated and tested for various applications. 

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated commercial production lines at CDIL Semiconductor, Mohali for discrete devices and Suchi Semicon, Surat for packaging. This has resulted in five operational commercial semiconductor ATMP units, alongside Micron, Kaynes, and CG Semi, out of the twelve approved units under Semicon 1.0.

Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi highlighted India’s execution velocity and macro resilience with 7.8% quarterly GDP growth, 3,000 km of operational dedicated freight corridors, a sovereign rating upgrade and a successful BRICS Summit hosted by India. Outlining the relentless momentum of the sector, the Prime Minister highlighted the expansion of the India Semiconductor Mission budget from USD 8 billion in Semicon 1.0 to USD 13.5 billion for Semicon 2.0.

Detailing the vision for a robust domestic supply chain, the Prime Minister urged leaders in equipment, chemicals, gases, and materials to capitalize on the golden opportunities presented by the twelve approved projects and an expanding demand pipeline. "We want the entire ecosystem to grow together,” asserted the Prime Minister. 

At the Conference, Secretary, MeitY, Shri S. Krishnan declared that India has "truly arrived" in the semiconductor space, announcing the transition to Semicon 2.0 after committing its initial six-year funding phase in just four years. 

MoUs and Strategic Announcements

Strategic MoUs and announcements spanning design, fabrication, packaging, materials, equipment and skills involved Tata Electronics, Kaynes Semicon, Intel, Nexperia, CDIL Semiconductors and their partners. Key outcomes included India's first commercial QFN chip by Suchi Semicon and eInfochips, integration of the India-designed SenseSoC-200 chip into smart meters, six ChipIN Regional Centres and HORIBA India's KOACH Experience Centre.

Addressing the media, Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw outlined ‘Semicon 2.0’, marking India’s transition from foundational credibility to comprehensive domestic capability.

India–USA Country Roundtable – Semiconductor & Electronics Ecosystem

The India-USA Country Roundtable brought together government and industry representatives from 64 Indian companies and 52 international organisations. Discussions focused on commercial partnerships, joint ventures, R&D, supply chains and skills across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

India–Japan Semiconductor Roundtable

The India-Japan Semiconductor Roundtable focused on combining Japan's strengths in equipment, materials and precision manufacturing with India's demand, design talent and expanding manufacturing base through joint ventures, technology transfers, localized supply chains and R&D.

Focused Sessions

The opening day featured focused sessions charting India’s transition from foundational policy planning to large-scale execution across the silicon value chain. These sessions covered AI-enabled chip design and manufacturing, advanced packaging, next-generation manufacturing, equipment R&D and workforce development. 

SEMICON India 2026 which runs till September 19th at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, features more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers. The exhibition features six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
item.description: Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel and Former Delhi Mayor Shri Jai Prakash Inaugurate ‘Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ ‘Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ to be Celebrated Nationwide Till October 17 “Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026 Will Carry Forward the Resolve of 25 Years of Service and Good Governance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi through Jan Bhagidari”: KVIC Chairman KVIC Disburses ₹289 Crore Margin Money Subsidy to 3,366 PMEGP Beneficiaries; Five Digital Initiatives Launched Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:28PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel and Former Delhi Mayor Shri Jai Prakash Inaugurate ‘Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026’
‘Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ to be Celebrated Nationwide Till October 17
“Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026 Will Carry Forward the Resolve of 25 Years of Service and Good Governance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi through Jan Bhagidari”: KVIC Chairman
KVIC Disburses ₹289 Crore Margin Money Subsidy to 3,366 PMEGP Beneficiaries; Five Digital Initiatives Launched
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, inaugurated the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026" on Thursday, marking the birth anniversary of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, from the KVIC campus at Gandhi Darshan, Rajghat. The commemoration will be celebrated nationwide from September 17 to October 17, 2026, with public participation. The chief guest, Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman, KVIC, inaugurated the event. On the occasion, former Delhi Mayor Shri Jai Prakash, representatives of Khadi institutions, artisans, PMEGP beneficiaries, trainees, officers and employees of KVIC, as well as artisans and other participants who joined online from across the country, were present. During the event, the artisans cut a cake with #AshirwadKaDiya and lit 25 lamps of "Sankalp se Siddhi" to symbolize Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of service, good governance, and public participation.

Shri Goyal said that service, good governance, and public participation have been key principles ​​in Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of public life. Inspired by this spirit, KVIC will spread the message of Khadi, Swadeshi, employment, and self-reliance through the 'Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026'. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a symbol of self-respect, employment, rural economy, and Swadeshi. Under the Prime Minister's leadership, campaigns like 'Vocal for Local', 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', and 'Local to Global' have given a new identity to local products and rural entrepreneurship.

During the programme, machines and toolkits were distributed to artisans from Delhi and the North East regions. Shri Goyal said that these are not just equipment, but new opportunities for employment, self-reliance, and respect for artisans. Margin money subsidy of ₹289 crore was also disbursed under the PMEGP. This will establish 3,366 new projects across the country and create employment opportunities for approximately 37,026 people. Bank loans worth approximately ₹873 crore have been provided for these projects. At the event, 5,000 new PMEGP units were launched online. He said the objective of PMEGP is to transform youth, women, and rural entrepreneurs from job seekers to job creators.

The program marked the launch of the E-Commerce Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Mobile App, Hindi Vaibhav Portal, and KVIC Digital 2.0, aimed at making KVIC's digital services more accessible and effective. Also, 760 individual, group workshops, and renovated stores were inaugurated online across the country, and a Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition was organized. Activities such as the inauguration of a selfie point, a live demonstration of spinning the charkha, and the "Swadeshi Sankalp" campaign were also organized at the venue. Certificates were distributed to candidates trained in various skill development courses. Cleanliness activities were organized at the KVIC office complex at Gandhi Darshan, and Chairman, KVIC, Shri Manoj Goyal, planted a sapling, promoting environmental protection and a clean campus.

Under the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026," cleanliness drives, tree plantations, Khadi Yatras, the Swadeshi Sankalp pledge, awareness programs, artisan dialogues, and training programs will be organized across the country til 17th  October. Schools, villages, towns and Khadi institutions will be associated to these activities. Shri Goyal said that KVIC's effort is that this festival should not remain just a departmental programme but should become a campaign for the people and a festival of public participation. He said that there should be dialogue of Khadi in every school, talk of village industries in every village, talk of Swadeshi in every market.

Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav will also be linked with the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' campaign running from 17th September to 17th October. This year the theme of Swachhata Hi Seva campaign is 'Participation in Cleanliness, Clean India, Developed India'. Shri Goyal said, "Cleanliness is service, Swadeshi is service, providing employment is service, and respecting artisans is service." He called upon artisans, Khadi institutions, PMEGP beneficiaries, youth, and the KVIC family across the country to actively participate in the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026."

On this occasion, Shri Manoj Goyal opined that under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Khadi has achieved a new dimension. Today, Khadi has become a powerful medium to realize the resolve of Atmanirbhar Bharat, Vocal for Local, Local to Global, and Developed India 2047. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a source of livelihood for millions of artisans and weavers, a symbol of India's cultural heritage and sustainable development.

Khadi and Village Industries sector has made unprecedented progress due to  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's visionary thoughtfulness and policies, he added.  In the financial year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector exceeded ₹1.87 lakh crore, while the total income generated through this sector was ₹1.87 lakh crore. More than 20.4 million people are employed. He expressed confidence that the sector will achieve its target of ₹2.51 lakh crore in turnover in the coming years.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Food Processing Industries
‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ symbolises hope and self-reliance for beneficiaries
Union Minister Chirag Paswan interacts with beneficiaries at Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas in Thane
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi

The “Aashirwad Ka Diya” programme was organised at Niyojan Bhawan, District Collector’s Office, Thane, as part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas initiative of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries. The programme brought together farmers, FPO members, women beneficiaries, entrepreneurs, food-processing units and departmental representatives.

The programme was attended by Hon’ble Union Minister for Food Processing Industries Shri Chirag Paswan, Hon’ble Member of Parliament Shri Naresh Maske, Thane Deputy Mayor Shri Krushna Patil, along with Shri Preet Pal Singh, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries; Shri Krishna Panchal, Collector, Thane; Shri Ranjit Yadav, Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Parishad, Thane; Shri Remandeep Chowdhary, Director; Director, Agriculture Processing and Planning; District Superintendent of Agriculture, Thane; and senior departmental officials.

A key highlight was the direct interaction of Shri Chirag Paswan with beneficiaries of various Ministry initiatives, including PMFME, PMKSY and PLI. The Minister listened to their experiences and enquired about the impact of government support on their businesses and livelihoods, including the employment opportunities generated through their projects.

 

Food processing: a major opportunity

 

The programme also highlighted the immense potential of the food-processing sector. While India once faced limitations in food production, the country today has a strong and diverse agricultural production base, creating significant scope for processing, preservation and value addition.

 

The need of the hour is therefore to give greater impetus to food processing and build a strong and integrated value chain that connects farmers, FPOs, entrepreneurs, processors, industry and markets.

 

The emerging participation of entrepreneurs from both rural and urban India reflects this changing landscape. Entrepreneurs from different backgrounds are increasingly coming forward to establish food-processing enterprises and build products that represent the spirit of Brand Bharat.

‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ – a symbol of hope

 

The lighting of the “Aashirwad Ka Diya” was the central feature of the programme. The diya symbolised hope, opportunity, confidence and self-reliance in the lives of beneficiaries.

It represented the collective strength of the food-processing ecosystem—farmers producing quality raw material, FPOs bringing collective strength, women converting skills into enterprise, entrepreneurs undertaking processing and value addition, and industry providing technology, scale and market opportunities.

Beneficiaries shared their experiences and explained how government initiatives had helped them strengthen their enterprises, create employment and move towards greater economic self-reliance.

Maharashtra’s contribution acknowledged

 

Maharashtra has consistently played an important role in the implementation of initiatives of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries and in strengthening the participation of farmers, FPOs, women and entrepreneurs in the sector.

Shri Chirag Paswan expressed his pleasure at interacting with beneficiaries from Maharashtra and appreciated the opportunity to work with the state’s farmers, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders.

The programme reinforced the message of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas—that the true purpose of public service is realised when opportunities created through government initiatives reach people and translate into enterprise, employment, value addition and better livelihoods.

The “Aashirwad Ka Diya” thus became a symbol of a larger vision: to transform India’s agricultural strength into greater value, stronger enterprises and new opportunities, while carrying the light of entrepreneurship and self-reliance to more families across the country.

****

CMC – Media

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission inaugurates 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week with focus on rational use of medicines
6th National Pharmacovigilance Week to be observed across the country from 17–23 September 2026  
Week-long campaign to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and public on Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:11PM by PIB Delhi

The 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week (NPW) was inaugurated at the Padmashri Nitya Anand Auditorium Hall, ALRC Building, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ghaziabad, today.  IPC serves as the National Coordination Centre for the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC-PvPI). Being observed from 17–23 September 2026 across the country, the 6th NPW is themed “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance – A Step Towards Safer Healthcare”. The week-long campaign aims to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and the public about the importance of adverse drug reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR (virtually); Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC; Dr. Jai Prakash, Officer-in-Charge, PvPI; Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, IHBAS; Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, MoHFW; and along with other dignitaries and stakeholders.

Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), stressed the importance of building adequate capacity to verify, assess and analyse safety reports, enabling pharmacovigilance data to effectively inform regulatory and clinical actions.

Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, Ghaziabad, in his remarks, highlighted the need to strengthen the pharmacovigilance network at the grassroots level, with an aspiration for every Aspirational District to have at least one ADR Monitoring Centre (AMC) and one Medical Device Monitoring Centre (MDMC). He also emphasised greater utilisation of pharmacovigilance data, including exploring opportunities for drug repurposing and using safety data to support and promote the rational use of medicines.

The inaugural session also featured remarks by Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, Institute of Human Behaviour & Allied Sciences (IHBAS), New Delhi; Dr. Abdul Nasser, Cardiac Anaesthesiologist, Max Hospital, Vaishali; and Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India. Video messages were delivered by Shri Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner, FDA Maharashtra and Dr. Shanthi Pal, Team Lead, Pharmacovigilance, World Health Organization (WHO).

A key highlight of the programme was the release of Volume 16, Issue 2 (2026) of the PvPI Newsletter, reflecting the programme’s continued efforts towards strengthening pharmacovigilance, promoting rational medicine use and enhancing public awareness on medicine safety.

The technical sessions focused on strengthening medication and patient safety. Prof. Sangeeta Sharma spoke on “Pharmacovigilance and Rational Use of Medicines: Two Pillars of Medication Safety”, while Dr. Abdul Nasser addressed “Beyond Medicines: Role of MvPI in Strengthening Patient Safety”, highlighting the complementary role of pharmacovigilance and materiovigilance.

The 6th NPW reinforces the call for greater ADR reporting and the effective use of pharmacovigilance data to promote safer and rational use of medicines.

****

SR

P. Singh Baghel An Interaction Program with Beneficiaries of the PM 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme was Held at NDDB, Anand Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Ahmedabad Under the joint aegis of the Union Ministry of Panchayati…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
Central Government is Committed to the Equitable Development of Every Region and State in the Country: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh
25 Years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Public Life are Like a Golden Era of Development and Transformation for the Country: Union Minister of State Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel
An Interaction Program with Beneficiaries of the PM 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme was Held at NDDB, Anand
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Ahmedabad

Under the joint aegis of the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj and the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, a special interaction program with beneficiaries of the 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme, as well as a property card distribution ceremony under the SVAMITVA scheme, was held today at the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) Auditorium in Anand.

Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh was specially present as the Chief Guest, and Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel was present as the Special Guest on this occasion.

Speaking at the program, Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated that the entire life of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has been dedicated to the service of Mother India. During his successful tenure as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, he accomplished the monumental task of bringing Narmada waters to every corner, permanently solving the state's major water problem. It was due to this journey of development and popularity that the people of the country entrusted him with the leadership of the nation in 2014. Today, under the Prime Minister's leadership, India is moving forward with the resolve to become a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. The Central Government is committed to the equitable development of every region and state of the country. Uniting all states into a single thread without any political discrimination to make the country self-reliant is the main objective of the Prime Minister.

The Union Minister further stated that property-related issues were the biggest cause of violence and disputes in rural areas. Owing to the Prime Minister's foresight, the 'SVAMITVA Scheme' was launched, under which title deeds (cards) for their land/properties are handed over to villagers through drone surveys. Currently, more than 3 crore SVAMITVA cards have been distributed across the country. On the basis of these cards, villagers can now easily obtain loans from banks, freeing them from exploitation by usurers. The work on the second phase of this scheme across the country, including Gujarat, is in its final stage, which is proving to be a blessing in bringing social harmony and economic prosperity to villages.

Outlining the development in the fisheries sector, the Minister stated that the livelihood of approximately 6 crore people in the country is connected with the fisheries sector. After 2014, the Central Government took historic decisions for this sector, such as the Blue Revolution, PM MSY (PM Matsya Sampada Yojana), and the creation of a separate Ministry of Fisheries. Despite global economic challenges and tariff issues, under the guidance of the Prime Minister, this sector has been taken to new heights by formulating policies for Free Trade Agreements (FTA) and deep-sea fishing.

On this occasion, Union Minister of State Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel stated that the 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's public life are not merely a period of time, but are like a golden era of development and transformation for the country. After making Gujarat a role model as its Chief Minister, he has brought light into the lives of crores of citizens across the country as Prime Minister through various schemes such as poverty alleviation, electricity, housing, toilets, Ayushman Card, Mudra Scheme, and PM-KISAN. He proved that service to the nation is paramount. Because of his governance, India is today moving towards the 'Golden Era of Indian Politics'.

The Minister stated that the 'SVAMITVA Scheme' and the 'Blue Revolution' have brought a revolutionary transformation in the upliftment of rural India. By providing property cards under the SVAMITVA scheme, ownership rights have been granted in rural areas, bringing an end to land disputes and domestic quarrels between brothers, as well as making it easier for people to receive financial assistance.

During the event, property cards were distributed to rural beneficiaries under the 'SVAMITVA' scheme at the hands of dignitaries. Along with this, direct interactions were held with beneficiaries of the fisheries scheme and the SVAMITVA card scheme to discuss the benefits of government schemes. Beneficiaries of the SVAMITVA scheme and PM Matsya Sampada Yojana also presented their experiences regarding the benefits they received.

The program was attended in large numbers by Chairman of the National Dairy Development Board Dr. Meenesh Shah, Joint Secretary of the Panchayati Raj Department Shri Amit Agrawal, Director Dharmendra Ji, District Development Officer Ms. Devahuti, officials of the district administration, as well as beneficiaries of the Matsya Sampada Scheme and SVAMITVA Scheme.

SM/IJ/JD

(Release ID: 2311716)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Organises Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign in Budaun Uttar Pradesh
Union Minister of State Shri B. L. Verma Highlights Dignity, Safety And Empowerment Of Sanitation Workers
PPE Kits, Ayushman Cards And Auto-Rickshaw Keys Distributed Among Safai Mitras
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, organised the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign at the DIET Auditorium in Budaun, Uttar Pradesh, today with the objective of promoting the message, ‘Honour for Safai Mitras, Resolve for Swachh Bharat’.

Addressing the gathering, the Chief Guest Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma highlighted the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, which seeks to ensure the dignity and safety of sanitation workers and empower them socially and economically.

He informed that 90,157 sewer and septic tank workers have been profiled under the Scheme. Of these, 87,078 have received personal protective equipment (PPE) kits and 76,920 have been covered under health insurance.

The Minister further stated that 5,00,013 waste pickers have been profiled, of whom 3,15,593 have been validated. A total of 1,79,269 waste pickers have been provided PPE kits.

Shri Verma informed that in Budaun, 146 sewer and septic tank workers and 339 waste pickers have been validated through the profiling process.

During the programme, PPE kits were symbolically presented by Shri Verma to 40 sewer and septic tank workers and 30 waste pickers. In addition, Ayushman cards were also distributed among 31 SafaiMitras, while six Safai Mitras received keys of auto-rickshaws.

The programme reaffirmed the Government's commitment to ‘Vanchiton Ko Variyata’ - giving priority to the deprived - by ensuring that people who have historically remained underserved or overlooked receive the assistance and support to which they are entitled. This focus on those at the margins reflects the Government's broader vision of Viksit Bharat, in which every citizen has an opportunity to contribute to and benefit from India's development journey.

Among those present were Shri Rajeev Singh, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Dataganj; Shri Harish Chandra, Member of the Legislative Assembly, Bilsi; Shri Vagish Pathak, Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council; Smt. Varsha Yadav, Chairperson, Zila Panchayat, Budaun; and Shri Prabhat Kumar Singh, Managing Director, National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation.

PR-124- TAR/KV/GA/RK

The initiative places emphasis on making cleanliness a collective responsibility, encouraging officers and staff to maintain clean…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Land Resources Launches Swachhata Hi Seva with Emphasis on Cleanliness as a Collective Responsibility
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, has commenced the Swachhata Hi Seva initiative from 17 September 2026, reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness, responsible waste management and a culture of public service.

The initiative places emphasis on making cleanliness a collective responsibility, encouraging officers and staff to maintain clean offices and surroundings and to contribute actively towards a cleaner environment. The focus extends beyond workplace cleanliness to individual and community-level practices that can help reduce littering and improve sanitation.

Addressing the importance of cleanliness and public participation, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, said, “Swachhata is not only about cleaning our surroundings; it is about taking responsibility for the spaces we share. The real impact of Swachhata Hi Seva will come when each one of us makes cleanliness a part of our everyday conduct. By preventing litter, keeping our workplaces and neighbourhoods clean, and ensuring that waste is responsibly managed, we can contribute meaningfully to a cleaner and healthier India.”

The Department has called upon its officers and staff to actively participate in cleanliness activities and adopt simple, sustainable practices in their daily lives. The initiative encourages individuals to take ownership of their immediate surroundings rather than leaving the responsibility of cleanliness solely to sanitation workers.

The programme also highlights the importance of responsible handling of plastic waste and e-waste. Employees have been encouraged to identify unused items at home and in offices and explore avenues for their reuse, repair, recycling or responsible disposal, thereby contributing to a circular economy.

The initiative further underscores that cleanliness is intrinsically linked with public service. The message is to reduce the generation of waste, avoid littering and support systems that enable waste to be recycled and reused. The speech also highlighted examples of plastic waste being recycled into useful products, demonstrating the potential of responsible waste management and circular practices.

The Department has urged its personnel to lead by example by maintaining clean workspaces, keeping their surroundings free from litter and encouraging similar practices within their homes and communities.

Swachhata Hi Seva seeks to reinforce the idea that cleanliness is a shared responsibility and that small individual actions, when adopted collectively, can contribute to a larger transformation. The initiative is aligned with the broader vision of promoting responsible citizenship, public service and sustainable practices.

*******

RC/HR

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Lights ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ With Persons In Recovery On Seva Diwas
Ceremony Under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan Highlights Government’s Commitment To Prevention, Treatment, Rehabilitation And Social Reintegration Of Persons Affected By Substance Dependence
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment organised a special ceremony under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan on the occasion of Seva Diwas at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, in National Capital here today.

As part of the ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ initiative, Union Minister of Social Justice & Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, lit the ceremonial Diya alongside persons who have successfully undergone treatment and rehabilitation for substance dependence.

The ceremony conveyed a strong message of hope, dignity, resilience and recovery to persons affected by substance dependence and their families while reaffirming the Government’s commitment to reducing the demand for drugs and strengthening prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration efforts.

Around 250 persons in recovery, who had received treatment and rehabilitation support through Grant-in-Aid Institutions of the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (DoSJE) functioning in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas, joined the Union Minister in the ceremony.

Their participation symbolized the possibilities of recovery and reintegration and highlighted the importance of timely professional treatment, sustained rehabilitation, family support and community participation in enabling persons affected by substance dependence to rebuild their lives with dignity and return to productive participation in society.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Virendra Kumar reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to strengthening efforts for prevention of substance abuse, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

He said the journey of recovery is a journey of hope, courage and a new beginning. Through initiatives such as ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’, we seek to reinforce the message that persons who have overcome substance dependence deserve dignity, acceptance and every opportunity to rebuild their lives, he added.

Dr Kumar said a supportive family and community environment, combined with professional treatment and sustained rehabilitation, can play a decisive role in the journey towards recovery and social reintegration.

The Minister emphasized the importance of creating an enabling and stigma-free environment in which persons in recovery are supported by their families and communities and provided opportunities to lead dignified and productive lives.

The lighting of the ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ alongside persons in recovery served as a symbolic expression of hope, renewal and a fresh beginning. It underscored the message that recovery is possible and that sustained care, professional intervention, family support and collective community action are important components of the rehabilitation process.

The ceremony formed part of the broader Seva Sankalp Abhiyan being undertaken across the country on Seva Diwas. The initiative reflects the Government’s emphasis on service-oriented, inclusive and people-centric governance, with dignity, empowerment and social inclusion at the centre of welfare interventions.

During the programme, Dr. Virendra Kumar also visited an exclusive exhibition of original paintings depicting the life and journey of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, being held at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre.

The exhibition presenting the Prime Minister’s journey through a collection of 76 original artworks portraying various facets and milestones of his public life, is being held for six days and will remain open until 20th of this month.

Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Director Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, DAIC Director Shri Akash Patil, senior officers of the Ministry, cross section of people, civil society members and other stakeholders were also present on the occasion.

Through its programmes for prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment continues to work towards strengthening institutional support for persons affected by substance dependence and facilitating their return to dignified and productive lives.

PR-124-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda Addresses World Patient Safety Day 2026 Event at Dr. RML Hospital
Ayushman Bharat Has Enabled 11.5 Crore Beneficiaries to Access Treatment Worth Around ₹1.6 Lakh Crore: Union Health Minister
Jan Aushadhi Has Enabled Citizens to Save Around ₹45,000 Crore on Medicines: Shri Nadda
A Clean Hospital is Also a Safer Hospital: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda on World Patient Safety Day
Quality & Safety Handbook Released at RML Hospital to Strengthen Patient Safety Practices
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of World Patient Safety Day 2026, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda addressed an event organised at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, today. The event highlighted the Government’s continued efforts towards strengthening patient safety as an integral component of quality healthcare and health-system strengthening.

The theme for World Patient Safety Day 2026, “Safe care for noncommunicable diseases”, with the slogan “Safe care for life!”, highlights the importance of safe, coordinated and continuous care for people living with noncommunicable diseases (NCDs).

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda said that 17 September is a significant day as it brings together the themes of public service, patient safety and cleanliness. He also conveyed his greetings and best wishes to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday, noting that the occasion is an opportunity to acknowledge his contribution to public service and his continued commitment to the service of the nation. He expressed his wishes for the Prime Minister’s long, healthy life and continued service to the country.

Speaking on World Patient Safety Day, Shri Nadda said that patient safety is an extremely important component of healthcare and that the objective of healthcare delivery must extend beyond treatment to ensuring that every patient receives safe, high-quality, dignified and patient-centric care. He appreciated ABVIMS & Dr. RML Hospital for organising the programme and particularly commended the institution for bringing out the Quality & Safety Handbook, which provides a practical framework for strengthening quality and safety practices.

The Union Minister emphasised that patient safety requires the collective efforts of doctors, nurses, paramedical professionals, technicians, administrative personnel and other healthcare workers, along with patients and their attendants. He noted that safety and security of patients must remain central to healthcare delivery and that necessary precautions and protocols should not be compromised in the interest of speed. He stressed the importance of correct diagnosis, appropriate treatment, adherence to infection-prevention protocols and continuous attention to infection control.

Shri Nadda said that patient safety is closely linked with cleanliness and hygiene in healthcare facilities. Referring to the Swachhata movement, he highlighted the transformation of cleanliness into a people’s movement and emphasised that cleanliness should become a part of everyday habits and working practices. He noted that the creation of around 11 crore toilets over the past decade has significantly strengthened the country’s sanitation infrastructure and also contributed to dignity and improved living conditions.

The Union Minister said that the improvement in sanitation has also had an important bearing on public health outcomes, including a significant decline in diarrhoeal disease. He stressed that in hospitals, cleanliness has a direct connection with infection prevention and patient safety. He called for collective responsibility towards hand hygiene, proper waste disposal, adherence to infection-control protocols and maintaining hospital premises and facilities responsibly. He emphasised that a clean hospital is not merely a well-maintained hospital, but also a safer hospital.

Highlighting the importance of institutional quality assurance, Shri Nadda said that the National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) certification was introduced in 2015 to establish nationally recognised standards for assessing the quality of healthcare institutions. He noted that 60,000 government health facilities are now NQAS-certified and said that efforts are underway to further increase the number of certified institutions, with a target of taking the coverage to around 2 lakh institutions. He emphasised that the expansion of quality standards and certification reflects the continued focus on institutionalising quality, safety and patient-centric care across the public health system.

Shri Nadda also highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat in strengthening financial protection and access to healthcare. He said that under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries are provided health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care. He said that Ayushman Bharat has emerged as one of the world’s largest health coverage programmes and has enabled millions of people to access treatment without facing the burden of catastrophic healthcare expenditure.

The Union Minister stated that approximately 11.5 crore beneficiaries have received treatment under Ayushman Bharat, with treatment worth of around ₹1.6 lakh crore. He said that the programme has enabled families, including elderly citizens, to access procedures and treatments that might otherwise have imposed a substantial financial burden on them.

Highlighting the role of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), Shri Nadda said that the initiative has expanded access to quality generic medicines at affordable prices. He noted that more than 20,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been established across the country and that efforts are underway to expand this network further to around 25,000 outlets, while also increasing the range of medicines and ensuring their timely availability and quality. He also highlighted the substantial savings available on certain cancer medicines and said that the cumulative savings to citizens through Jan Aushadhi have been estimated at around ₹45,000 crore.

Shri Nadda further highlighted the importance of reducing out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare. He noted that the share of out-of-pocket expenditure in total health expenditure has declined from around 62 per cent in 2014 to around 43 per cent, and emphasised that continued efforts are being made to reduce the financial burden on families.

The Union Minister also highlighted the importance of preventive healthcare, early detection and continuity of care. He referred to the strengthening of vaccination, maternal and child health services and screening for noncommunicable diseases. He noted that vaccination is being digitally tracked from childhood and that mechanisms are in place to ensure follow-up with beneficiaries and families so that due vaccinations are completed.

Shri Nadda said that screening and early detection of noncommunicable diseases are also being strengthened through the public health system. He highlighted screening for conditions including diabetes, hypertension and various cancers, including oral, cervical and breast cancer, and said that tens of crores of people have been screened under the ongoing efforts.

Emphasising the broader meaning of patient safety, Shri Nadda said that patients entering a hospital bring not only an illness but also anxiety, hope and expectations. He noted that the conduct of healthcare personnel—including timely information, appropriate guidance, reassurance and support—is an integral part of the patient experience.

Shri Nadda congratulated ABVIMS & Dr. RML Hospital for its initiatives on World Patient Safety Day and appreciated its efforts towards strengthening quality and safety through systematic audits, training, continuous monitoring and institutional learning. He said that such efforts contribute to building a healthcare system in which safety, quality, affordability and dignity remain central to every patient’s experience.

Speaking at the Occasion, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, said that maintaining a clean hospital environment is essential for ensuring safe and quality care. She highlighted that ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital has achieved NABH accreditation, reflecting its adherence to established standards of patient safety and quality of treatment. She stressed that cleanliness in hospitals cannot be the responsibility of healthcare workers alone and requires active participation from patients, visitors and attendants as well. She said that the convergence of ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ and World Patient Safety Day provides an opportunity to reinforce collective responsibility towards hygiene, infection prevention and safe healthcare.

Smt. Srivastava highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to make healthcare accessible, affordable and of high quality for every citizen. Referring to the Swasth Nari, Sashakt Parivar campaign launched last year, she noted that more than 17 lakh health camps were organised across the country, with participation of over 11 crore people. She also highlighted key initiatives including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme, expansion of vaccination services, PM-ABHIM, eSanjeevani, PM-JAY and Ayushman Vay Vandana, which are strengthening access to preventive and curative healthcare. She further emphasised the importance of affordable medicines in reducing the overall cost of treatment and highlighted the role of Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras and AMRIT Pharmacies, including the AMRIT Pharmacy at RML Hospital, in improving access to affordable medicines and implants.

Emphasising the importance of patient-centric healthcare, Secretary, Department of Pharmaceuticals, Shri Manoj Joshi said that sustained efforts over the past 10–12 years have focused on improving patient satisfaction and making quality healthcare more accessible, particularly for economically vulnerable sections of society. He highlighted the crucial role of initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) and Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) in making quality treatment more accessible and affordable by strengthening financial protection and improving access to affordable medicines. He also underlined that maintaining cleanliness in hospitals remains a significant challenge and called for sustained and collective efforts to strengthen hygiene, cleanliness and infection-control practices, which are integral to ensuring safe and patient-centric care.

Furthermore, A Quality & Safety Handbook of ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital was also released during the programme. The Handbook provides healthcare staff with practical and standardised operational guidance to support best practices, augment quality of care and strengthen adherence to patient-safety protocols across different operational areas of the hospital.

During the event, Shri Nadda also interacted with the beneficiaries of Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) and Jan Ayushadhi Pariyojana.

About Government Efforts for Patient Safety

The Government has been strengthening patient safety through a coordinated approach focused on institutional strengthening, capacity building, knowledge sharing, peer learning and continuous quality improvement. The National Patient Safety Secretariat (NPSS) under the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, is facilitating these efforts, including through the India Patient Safety Network (IPSN) comprising 20 AIIMS and 5 Institutes of National Importance (INIs). The Network provides a platform for healthcare institutions to share experiences, identify and disseminate good practices and strengthen patient-safety systems through evidence-based solutions and cross-learning.

The emphasis on learning from institutional experiences and translating them into action was also reflected in the National Conference on Patient Safety 2026, held on 11–12 September 2026 at AIIMS Nagpur. Organised by AIIMS Nagpur in collaboration with NPSS, DGHS and MoHFW, the two-day Conference brought together more than 100 faculty experts and over 450 delegates from medical colleges and healthcare institutions across the country. Senior representatives from various AIIMS and other institutions, along with experts from ICMR, NABH, NABL, AYUSH, National Health Programmes and the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI), participated in scientific deliberations and shared institutional innovations and good practices.

The national focus on strengthening patient safety is also being advanced through the National Action Plan for Patient Safety (NAPPS) 2030, being developed through NPSS. Building upon the National Patient Safety Implementation Framework (NPSIF) 2018–25, the proposed framework seeks to strengthen patient safety across healthcare settings, with priority areas including medication, surgical, blood, medical device, laboratory and diagnostic, infection, vaccine and injection, facility and AYUSH patient safety, along with operational research and patient, family and caregiver engagement.

Reflecting this broader approach at the institutional level, ABVIMS & Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital marked World Patient Safety Day by undertaking a month-long, hospital-wide closed-loop audit campaign under the theme, “Measure, Master, Maintain: Elevate Patient Safety at Every Level.” The initiative brought together clinical and operational departments in a structured three-stage process of Baseline Audit, Rapid Corrective Implementation through Training and Verification Audit, with the objective of identifying gaps, undertaking corrective measures and verifying improvements in patient-safety practices.

The focus on patient safety is also complemented by activities undertaken under the Swachhata Hi Seva Abhiyaan, reinforcing the importance of cleanliness, hygiene and well-maintained healthcare environments in creating safe and patient-friendly spaces for patients, families and healthcare workers.

Regular capacity-building initiatives, including master training programmes, orientation of healthcare professionals and patient-safety nodal teams, webinars, institutional sensitisation and technical engagements, are being undertaken to strengthen competencies, promote a culture of safety and support learning from patient-safety incidents.

The Government’s approach is to embed patient safety within routine healthcare delivery, institutional quality improvement and healthcare governance. On World Patient Safety Day, the Ministry reaffirms its commitment to working with States and Union Territories, healthcare institutions, healthcare professionals, patients, families and other stakeholders to strengthen a coordinated and learning-oriented patient-safety ecosystem and ensure safe, timely, coordinated and quality care throughout every patient’s healthcare journey.

*****

SR

HFW/ HFM addresses on World Patient Safety Day /17 September 2026/3

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Seva Sankalp Abhiyan Reflects Spirit of Citizen-Centric Governance and Nation-Building: Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari
‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ Symbolises the Bond of Service, Gratitude and Citizens’ Participation: Shri Gadkari
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:31PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today said that ‘Seva Bhava’ is the guiding spirit of public service and development, with Government initiatives aimed at improving the quality of life of citizens and ensuring that the benefits of development reach the last mile.

Addressing the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan – Aashirwad Ka Diya’ virtually, Shri Gadkari said that the occasion of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday provides an opportunity to renew the collective resolve towards serving the people and contributing to the nation’s development.

The Minister said that infrastructure development is ultimately about serving citizens and creating better opportunities for them. Roads and highways are not merely physical assets; they connect people with schools, hospitals, markets, workplaces and other essential services. Improved connectivity saves time, facilitates movement of agricultural produce, supports tourism and generates new avenues of employment and economic activity.

Highlighting initiatives such as PM GatiShakti, Shri Gadkari said that integrated infrastructure planning and modern highway development are transforming connectivity across the country. Projects in difficult and hilly areas, including Zojila Tunnel and other all-weather connectivity initiatives, are helping connect remote communities with essential services and opportunities.

He said that the spirit of Seva extends across sectors, with initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat reflecting the Government’s focus on improving access to essential services and enhancing citizens’ well-being.

Shri Gadkari emphasised that development must be time-bound, result-oriented, transparent and quality-driven. He stressed the adoption of world-class technology, reduction of import dependence, efficient use of resources and strict accountability for substandard work and malpractices.

The Minister also highlighted the Government’s efforts towards safe, affordable and sustainable mobility, including electric vehicles, alternative fuels, biofuels and hydrogen-based technologies, along with strengthening public transport.

He said that the real measure of development is the positive difference it makes in the everyday lives of citizens—the time saved, services made accessible, opportunities created and communities connected.

Shri Gadkari said that the ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ initiative symbolises the spirit of Seva Sankalp—a collective commitment to serve the people with dedication, integrity and a citizen-first approach.

He conveyed his greetings and good wishes to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday and reaffirmed the commitment to continue the journey of citizen-centric development, quality infrastructure and responsive public service. He expressed confidence that, under the visionary and guiding leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India will continue to advance towards becoming a Vishwaguru and realise the vision of a strong, prosperous and Viksit Bharat.

***

GDH/DS

Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain additional shareholding in Azure Power Global Limited by OMERS Infrastructure Asia Holdings Pte. Ltd.
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of certain additional shareholding in Azure Power Global Limited by OMERS Infrastructure Asia Holdings Pte. Ltd.

The Proposed Combination envisages acquisition of certain additional shareholding in Azure Power Global Limited (Target) by OMERS Infrastructure Asia Holdings Pte. Ltd. (Acquirer) from CDPQ Infrastructures Asia Pte. Ltd.

The Acquirer is an investment entity of OMER Administration Corporation (OAC). OAC is the administrator of Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System Primary Pension Plan (OMERS) and trustee of pension funds. OMERS is one of Canada’s largest multi-employers defined benefit pension plans with over 1,000 participating employers.

The Target is the parent entity of Azure group, which is engaged in setting up renewable energy plants, operating them and selling solar power in India.

Detailed order of the Commission will follow.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of certain equity share capital of Great White Global Pvt Ltd by ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III, Special Situation India Fund, others and related transactions
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of certain equity share capital of Great White Global Private Limited by ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III, Special Situation India Fund, Mr. Mehul Jadavji Shah, Ms. Julie Mehul Shah and Mehul Shah HUF and related transactions.

 

The proposed combination pertains to-

  1. the proposed acquisition of 50% of the issued and paid-up equity share capital of Great White Global Private Limited (Great White) by the ISAF III Onshore Fund, India Special Assets Fund III and Special Situation India Fund (collectively, EAAA Acquiring Entities) and Mr. Mehul Jadavji Shah, Ms. Julie Mehul Shah and Mehul Shah HUF (collectively, Continuing Promoter) (including through the Great White Holdings Private Limited (Acquisition SPV), to be implemented through a series of inter-connected steps, including the subsequent merger of the Acquisition SPV with and into Great White (Great White Transaction); and
  2. the proposed acquisition of sole control over ITVIS Innovations Private Limited (ITVIS) by Mr. Mehul Shah (ITVIS Transaction).

The Great White Transaction and the ITVIS Transaction are collectively referred to as the Proposed Combination.

The EAAA Acquiring Entities are schemes of irrevocable and contributory determinate trusts registered with Securities and Exchange Board of India as an alternative investment fund (AIF) / scheme of an AIF, and are managed by EAAA India Alternatives Limited (EAAA) in its capacity as their investment manager. EAAA is one of India’s leading multi-strategy alternative asset management platforms and is directly controlled by entities which are wholly owned subsidiaries of Edelweiss Financial Services Limited.

 

The Acquisition SPV is a private limited company incorporated in India recently, solely for the purpose of implementing the Proposed Transaction.

The Continuing Promoter comprise of Mr. Mehul Shah and Ms. Julie Shah, who are Indian resident individuals, and the Mehul Shah HUF.

Great White is primarily an Indian fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) and electrical infrastructure products company. It is also engaged in the manufacture and sale of beauty and personal care (BPC) products such as shaving blades, shaving foam, razors, shaving cream and aftershave lotion.

ITVIS is a private limited company incorporated in India and is engaged in the design, development, supply, and integration of intelligent lighting solutions, lighting automation products, smart electrical and sensor-based systems, and energy-efficient lighting technologies.

Detailed order of the Commission will follow.

*****

SR/ONP

item.content:encoded:
Competition Commission of India
CCI approves acquisition of three professional cricket franchises: Rajasthan Royals (India), Paarl Royals (South Africa) and Barbados Royals (Barbados) by Westview Cricket Ltd. and Poonawalla Sports and Fitness Pvt Ltd
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved acquisition of three professional cricket franchises: (i) Rajasthan Royals (India), (ii) Paarl Royals (South Africa) and (iii) Barbados Royals (Barbados) by Westview Cricket Limited and Poonawalla Sports and Fitness Private Limited.

The proposed combination pertains to the acquisition of three professional cricket franchises, (i) Rajasthan Royals (India), (ii) Paarl Royals (South Africa) and (iii) Barbados Royals (Barbados) by Westview Cricket Limited (Westview Cricket) and Poonawalla Sports and Fitness Private Limited (Poonawalla Sports).

Westview Cricket is a company registered in the United Kingdom.

Poonawalla Sports is a private limited company incorporated in India and is wholly owned by Mr. Adar Cyrus Poonawalla.

EM Sporting Holdings Limited (EMSH) is a private company limited by shares incorporated and registered in Mauritius. It is the holding company for Royal Multisport Private Limited (RMPL), Paarl Royals Ltd., and Barbados Royals Ltd. RMPL owns and operates the Rajasthan Royals franchise, which participates in the Indian Premier League T20 cricket tournament organized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

Detailed order of the Commission will follow.

*****

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance Department of Expenditure Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Institutionalize Swachhata, Clear Pending References Preparatory Phase Begins for Special Campaign 6.0; Implementation to Run Throughout October 2026 Department Reports Significant Pendency Reduction Since Special Campaign 5.0; Targets Set for Further Action in Campaign 6.0 Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Expenditure announced the launch of Special Campaign 6.0, a focused two‑phase drive to institutionalize Swachhata measures and expedite disposal of pending…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Expenditure Launches Special Campaign 6.0 to Institutionalize Swachhata, Clear Pending References
Preparatory Phase Begins for Special Campaign 6.0; Implementation to Run Throughout October 2026
Department Reports Significant Pendency Reduction Since Special Campaign 5.0; Targets Set for Further Action in Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Expenditure announced the launch of Special Campaign 6.0, a focused two‑phase drive to institutionalize Swachhata measures and expedite disposal of pending references across the Department and its attached organizations. The Preparatory Phase of the campaign will be conducted from 15th to 30th September 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

All Divisions of the Department along with organizations under its administrative control — Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Chief Adviser (Cost), Central Pension Accounting Office (CPAO), and Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) — have been sensitized to identify targets during the preparatory phase. Targets include cleanliness (Swachhata), space management, scrap disposal, record management, and early disposal of pending references. The structured preparatory arrangements are intended to ensure systematic, result‑oriented action during the Implementation Phase.

The Department reaffirmed its commitment to administrative efficiency and sustained cleanliness, noting the success of Special Campaign 5.0 (2nd to 31st October 2025). The momentum from the previous campaign continued beyond its formal period and contributed to measurable reductions in pendency. Between December 2025 and August 2026, the Department achieved the following disposal outcomes:

• MP references disposed: 57

• Comments furnished on Inter‑Ministerial References (Cabinet Note): 339

• State Government references addressed: 1,123

• Public grievances redressed: 2,788

• Public grievances appeals resolved: 141

The Department of Expenditure expressed confidence that Special Campaign 6.0 will further strengthen internal processes, enhance transparency, and improve service delivery. Officers and staff have been urged to actively participate in both phases and to adopt best practices for sustainable cleanliness and record management.

****

SR/SRI

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav celebrates Sewa Diwas with School Children, lights ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ under ‘Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan’
Posted On: 17 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav today interacted with school children in New Delhi on the occasion of Sewa Diwas, under the ‘Sewa Sankalp Abhiyan – Aashirwad Ka Diya’ programme. The event was graced by MLA (Mehrauli), Shri Gajender Yadav; Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Tanmay Kumar; Director General (Forest) and Special Secretary, MoEFCC, Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi besides senior officers of the Ministry.

The event was organized by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to commemorate 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s selfless service to the people of the country. It sought to promote the spirit of Sewa Bhav (selfless service) among communities, particularly the younger generation, while fostering awareness about forests, wildlife, nature and environmental conservation. The programme brought together school students, teachers, eco-club members, government officials and local communities.  As part of the programme, school children presented an environment-themed song.

A large Rangoli incorporating Diyas was prepared to symbolise light of knowledge, hope, service and environmental responsibility being carried forward by the younger generation. The Minister also reviewed an exhibition of selected paintings by school children, depicting themes related to environment, forests, wildlife and nature.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
